#' Sort a character vector and return the permutation index
#'
#' Internal helper used to keep labels aligned after alphabetical reordering.
#'
#' @param stringlist Character vector to sort.
#'
#' @return A list with the sorted vector (`sortlist`) and its permutation index (`perm`).
#' @keywords internal
sortPermute <- function(stringlist) {
  ord <- order(stringlist)
  sortlist <- stringlist[ord]
  perm <- ord
  return(list(sortlist = sortlist, perm = perm))
}

#' Read a cell-to-ligand compatibility matrix
#'
#' @param filename Path to a CSV file with cell types in rows and ligands in columns.
#'
#' @return A list containing the matrix plus ligand and cell-type labels.
#' @export
createCellLigList <- function(filename) {
  if (!file.exists(filename)) {
    print(filename)
    stop("ERROR: The file with cell-ligand interactions does not exist...")
  }
  
  df <- utils::read.csv(filename, row.names = 1)
  
  # Store the column names (ligands) and row names (cell types)
  ligands <- colnames(df)
  celltypes <- rownames(df)
  
  # Convert the data frame into a numeric matrix while removing rownames
  CellLigList = df %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Celltype") %>%
    dplyr::select(-Celltype) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
    as.matrix() 
  
  # Sort the cell types alphabetically and get the permutation indices
  sp <- sortPermute(celltypes)
  celltypes <- sp$sortlist # sorted cell type names
  perm <- sp$perm # permutation to reorder rows
  
  CellLigList <- CellLigList[perm, , drop = FALSE]
  
  return(list(CellLigList = CellLigList,
              ligands = ligands,
              celltypes = celltypes))
}

#' Read a cell-to-receptor compatibility matrix
#'
#' @param filename Path to a CSV file with cell types in rows and receptors in columns.
#'
#' @return A list containing the matrix plus receptor and cell-type labels.
#' @export
createCellRecList <- function(filename) {
  if (!file.exists(filename)) {
    stop("ERROR: The file with cell-receptor interactions does not exist...")
  }
  
  df <- utils::read.csv(filename, row.names = 1)
  
  # Store the column names (receptors) and row names (cell types)
  receptors <- colnames(df)
  celltypes <- rownames(df)

  # Convert the data frame into a numeric matrix while removing rownames
  CellRecList = df %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Celltype") %>%  # move rownames into a column
    dplyr::select(-Celltype) %>%                # remove the rowname column
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), as.numeric)) %>%  # convert all columns to numeric
    as.matrix()   

  # Sort the cell types alphabetically and get the permutation indices
  sp <- sortPermute(celltypes)
  celltypes <- sp$sortlist
  perm <- sp$perm
  
  CellRecList <- CellRecList[perm, , drop = FALSE]
  
  return(list(CellRecList = CellRecList,
              receptors = receptors,
              celltypes = celltypes))
}

#' Read and normalize cell-type abundance estimates
#'
#' @param cells Character vector of expected cell types.
#' @param filename Path to a CSV file containing patient-by-cell-type abundances.
#'
#' @return A list with the normalized `Dtypes` matrix plus labels.
#' @export
createCellTypeDistr <- function(cells, filename) {
  if (!file.exists(filename)) {
    stop("Cell type distribution file does not exist...")
  }
  
  # Read CSV file, using the first column as rownames (datasets)
  df <- utils::read.csv(filename, row.names = 1)
  
  # Extract column names as cell type names and row names as dataset/patient names
  celltypes <- colnames(df)
  datasets <- rownames(df)

  # Convert the data frame to a numeric matrix, keeping dataset names as rownames
  # so downstream functions (e.g. compute_racing_montecarlo) can recover patient IDs
  Dtypes <- as.matrix(df)
  storage.mode(Dtypes) <- "numeric"
  rownames(Dtypes) <- datasets

  # Normalize rows so each dataset sums to 1 (relative fractions)
  row_sums <- rowSums(Dtypes)
  normalized <- Dtypes / row_sums

  # Sort cell types alphabetically
  sp <- sortPermute(celltypes)
  celltypes <- sp$sortlist
  perm <- sp$perm
  Dtypes <- normalized[, perm, drop = FALSE]

  # Restrict to the cell types that actually appear in Lmatrix/Rmatrix.
  # ccc_table's expression threshold can leave some cell types with no
  # ligand/receptor pair at all (they never send or receive anything above
  # threshold), so `cells` (from Lmatrix) can be a strict subset of the
  # deconvolution's full cell-type vocabulary. Those cell types contribute
  # nothing to the network, so they're dropped from Cmatrix here rather than
  # left in as columns with no matching Lmatrix/Rmatrix row.
  if (length(cells) != length(celltypes)) {
    if (!all(cells %in% celltypes)) {
      stop("Cell types in Lmatrix/Rmatrix are not a subset of Cmatrix's cell types -- mismatched input files.")
    }
    keep <- celltypes %in% cells
    Dtypes <- Dtypes[, keep, drop = FALSE]
    celltypes <- celltypes[keep]
    Dtypes <- Dtypes / rowSums(Dtypes) # re-normalize so each dataset still sums to 1 after dropping cell types with no active ligand/receptor
  }

  return(list(Dtypes = Dtypes,
              celltypes = celltypes,
              datasets = datasets))
}

#' Read ligand-receptor interaction probabilities
#'
#' @param filename Path to a CSV file containing patient-by-interaction weights.
#' @param ligands Character vector of ligand names.
#' @param receptors Character vector of receptor names.
#'
#' @return A 3D array with dimensions ligand × receptor × patient.
#' @export
createInteractionDistr <- function(filename, ligands, receptors) {
  if (!file.exists(filename)) {
    stop("Interaction distribution file does not exist...")
  }
  
  df <- utils::read.csv(filename, row.names = 1)
  
  # Store column names (interaction names like LIG_REC) and row names (datasets)
  interactions <- colnames(df)
  datasets <- rownames(df)
  
  # Convert data frame to numeric matrix, replacing NA values with 0
  distr <- df %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Datasets") %>%
    dplyr::select(-Datasets) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(
      dplyr::everything(),                      # apply to all columns
      ~ tidyr::replace_na(as.numeric(.), 0)     # convert to numeric and replace NA with 0
    )) %>%
    as.matrix() 
  
  # Split interaction names "LIG_REC" into ligand and receptor parts
  parts <- strsplit(interactions, "_")
  rowWordIndex <- sapply(parts, `[`, 1)
  colWordIndex <- sapply(parts, `[`, 2)
  
  # Convert ligand/receptor names into numeric indices matching the provided ligand/receptor lists
  row <- match(rowWordIndex, ligands)
  col <- match(colWordIndex, receptors)
  
  # Create a 3D tensor to hold ligand-receptor probabilities
  # Dimensions: ligands x receptors x datasets
  DconnectionTensor <- array(0, dim = c(length(ligands), length(receptors), nrow(distr)))
  
  # Fill the tensor: for each dataset, assign probability values to the correct ligand-receptor pairs
  for (i in 1:nrow(distr)) {
    DconnectionTensor[cbind(row, col, i)] <- distr[i, ]
  }
  
  # Normalize each dataset slice so that the sum of all probabilities equals 1
  # This ensures that each dataset represents a valid probability distribution over all ligand-receptor pairs
  normsum <- apply(DconnectionTensor, 3, sum)
  
  for (i in 1:length(normsum)) {
    if (normsum[i] != 0) { # avoids division by 0
      DconnectionTensor[, , i] <- DconnectionTensor[, , i] / normsum[i]
    }
  }
  
  # Return the normalized 3D tensor
  return(DconnectionTensor)
}

#' Read a ligand-receptor sign matrix
#'
#' @param filename Path to a delimited file containing ligand-receptor signs or weights.
#'
#' @return A list with the numeric sign matrix and its ligand/receptor labels.
#' @export
Read_Lig_Rec_Interaction <- function(filename) {
  if (!file.exists(filename)) {
    stop("Interaction sign file does not exist...")
  }
  
  df <- data.table::fread(filename, header = TRUE)
  
  receptor_names <- colnames(df)[-1]
  ligand_names <- df[[1]]
  
  sign_matrix <- as.matrix(df[, -1])
  storage.mode(sign_matrix) <- "numeric"
  
  return(list(sign_matrix = sign_matrix,
              ligand_names = ligand_names,
              receptor_names = receptor_names))
}

#' Load RaCInG input matrices from disk --> Is there any normalization done here? I dont see it in the function
#'
#' Internal helper called by [prepare_input_files()] to read back the generated
#' CSV files and assemble the normalised matrices and 3-D tensor.
#' Users should call [prepare_input_files()] instead.
#'
#' @param file_name File stem used for the `Lmatrix_`, `Rmatrix_`, `Cmatrix_`, and
#'   `LRmatrix_` CSV files.
#' @param output_folder Directory containing the exported input files.
#' @param read_signs Logical; if `TRUE`, attempts to read `Sign_matrix_<file_name>.csv`
#'   from `output_folder`.
#'
#' @return A named list containing the input matrices and their labels.
#' @keywords internal
generateInput <- function(file_name, output_folder, read_signs = FALSE) {
  
  # -----------------------------
  # Read cell-to-ligand compatibility information
  # The function returns:
  #   CellLigList: numeric matrix indicating which cell type can interact with which ligand
  #   ligands: vector of ligand names
  #   celltypes: vector of cell type names (alphabetically sorted)
  # -----------------------------
  lig_path = paste0(output_folder, "Lmatrix_", file_name, ".csv")
  lig_data <- createCellLigList(lig_path)
  
  # -----------------------------
  # Read cell-to-receptor compatibility information
  # The function returns:
  #   CellRecList: numeric matrix indicating which cell type can interact with which receptor
  #   receptors: vector of receptor names
  #   celltypes: vector of cell type names (alphabetically sorted)
  # -----------------------------
  rec_path = paste0(output_folder, "Rmatrix_", file_name, ".csv")
  rec_data <- createCellRecList(rec_path)
  
  # -----------------------------
  # Read cell type distribution per dataset/patient
  # The function returns:
  #   Dtypes: matrix with relative abundance of each cell type per dataset (rows normalized)
  #   celltypes: vector of cell types
  #   datasets: vector of dataset/patient names
  # -----------------------------
  dist_path = paste0(output_folder, "Cmatrix_", file_name, ".csv")
  dist_data <- createCellTypeDistr(
    cells = lig_data$celltypes,
    filename = dist_path
  )
  
  # -----------------------------
  # Read ligand-receptor interaction weights
  # The function returns:
  #   DconnectionTensor: 3D array (ligands x receptors x datasets) of interaction probabilities
  # -----------------------------
  lr_path = paste0(output_folder, "LRmatrix_", file_name, ".csv")
  DconnectionTensor <- createInteractionDistr(
    filename = lr_path,
    ligands = lig_data$ligands,
    receptors = rec_data$receptors
  )
  
  # ----------------------------- TO BE CHECK THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SIGN MATRIX
  # Optionally read the sign of interactions (+1 stimulating, -1 inhibiting, 0 unknown)
  # If no sign matrix is supplied, fall back to zeros (unknown sign).
  # -----------------------------
  if (isTRUE(read_signs)) {
    sign_path <- file.path(output_folder, paste0("Sign_matrix_", file_name, ".csv"))
    if (!file.exists(sign_path)) {
      stop(
        "`read_signs = TRUE` requires a sign matrix file at ", sign_path,
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }
    sign_data <- Read_Lig_Rec_Interaction(sign_path)
    Sign_matrix <- sign_data$sign_matrix
  } else {
    Sign_matrix <- matrix(
      0,
      nrow = dim(DconnectionTensor)[1],
      ncol = dim(DconnectionTensor)[2]
    )
  }
  
  # -----------------------------
  # Return all input data in a list for use in the network generation model
  # -----------------------------
  return(list(
    Lmatrix = lig_data$CellLigList,       # cell-ligand compatibility matrix
    Rmatrix = rec_data$CellRecList,       # cell-receptor compatibility matrix
    Cmatrix = dist_data$Dtypes,                # normalized cell type distributions
    LRmatrix = DconnectionTensor,    # ligand-receptor interaction tensor
    celltypes = lig_data$celltypes,           # vector of cell type names
    ligands = lig_data$ligands,               # vector of ligand names
    receptors = rec_data$receptors,           # vector of receptor names
    Sign_matrix = Sign_matrix                  # matrix of interaction signs
  ))
}

#' Strip method/signature prefixes from deconvolution column names
#'
#' `multideconv::compute.deconvolution()` names its columns
#' `"{method}_{signature}_{celltype}"` (e.g. `"Quantiseq_TIL10_B.cells"`).
#' After `multideconv::standardize_celltype_colnames()` has normalized the
#' trailing cell-type portion to multideconv's canonical vocabulary, this
#' matches the longest canonical cell-type name each column ends with and
#' drops everything before it, leaving a short, method-agnostic label.
#' Columns that don't end in a recognized cell-type name are left unchanged.
#'
#' @param x Character vector of (already standardized) column names.
#'
#' @return A character vector of cleaned cell-type names, the same length as `x`.
#' @keywords internal
.clean_celltype_names <- function(x) {
  # Mirrors multideconv's internal canonical cell-type vocabulary.
  canonical <- c(
    "B.naive.cells", "B.memory.cells", "B.cells",
    "Macrophages.M0", "Macrophages.M1", "Macrophages.M2", "Macrophages.cells",
    "Monocytes", "Neutrophils",
    "NK.activated", "NK.resting", "NK.cells", "NKT.cells",
    "CD4.memory.activated", "CD4.memory.resting", "CD4.naive",
    "CD4.non.regulatory", "CD4.regulatory", "CD4.cells", "CD8.cells",
    "T.cells.helper", "T.cells.gamma.delta",
    "Dendritic.activated.cells", "Dendritic.resting.cells", "Dendritic.cells",
    "Cancer", "Endothelial", "Eosinophils", "Plasma", "Myocytes",
    "Fibroblasts", "Mast.activated.cells", "Mast.resting.cells", "Mast.cells",
    "CAF", "uncharacterized_cell"
  )
  canonical <- canonical[order(-nchar(canonical))]  # longest match wins

  vapply(x, function(nm) {
    hit <- canonical[endsWith(nm, canonical)]
    if (length(hit) > 0) hit[1] else nm
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

#' Estimate per-cell-type average expression profiles from one composition
#'
#' For each gene, solves a non-negative least squares regression of bulk TPM
#' expression across samples against per-sample cell-type fractions, giving
#' one expression value per gene per cell type:
#' `bulk_expr[gene, sample] ~= sum_celltype fractions[sample, celltype] * profile[gene, celltype]`.
#' Valid only when every column of `deconv` already belongs to one coherent
#' composition (fractions summing to ~1 per sample). When `deconv` instead
#' spans multiple deconvolution methods/signatures concatenated together (as
#' `multideconv::compute.deconvolution()` produces before subgroup analysis),
#' use [.estimate_expression_profiles_subgroups()] instead -- fitting NNLS
#' directly across method/signature blocks here would violate the mixture
#' equation this regression assumes.
#'
#' @param counts_tpm Gene-by-sample TPM matrix.
#' @param deconv Sample-by-cell-type fraction matrix.
#'
#' @return A gene-by-cell-type data frame of estimated expression profiles.
#' @keywords internal
.estimate_expression_profiles_samples <- function(counts_tpm, deconv) {
  samples <- intersect(colnames(counts_tpm), rownames(deconv))
  X <- as.matrix(deconv[samples, , drop = FALSE])
  Y <- as.matrix(counts_tpm[, samples, drop = FALSE])

  profile <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(Y), ncol = ncol(X),
                    dimnames = list(rownames(Y), colnames(X)))
  for (g in seq_len(nrow(Y))) {
    profile[g, ] <- stats::coef(nnls::nnls(X, Y[g, ]))
  }

  as.data.frame(profile)
}

#' Estimate per-cell-type expression profiles across multiple deconvolution
#' methods/signatures
#'
#' `multideconv::compute.deconvolution()`'s raw output concatenates one block
#' of columns per method-signature combination (named
#' `"{method}_{signature}_{celltype}"`). Each block is, on its own, a valid
#' composition -- multideconv itself verifies every block's standardized
#' cell-type columns sum to 1 per sample -- but
#' `multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()`'s merged "Deconvolution
#' matrix" is not: it stitches together representatives from different blocks
#' per cell type, so fitting [.estimate_expression_profiles_samples()]'s NNLS
#' mixture equation directly on it is invalid. This instead fits one profile
#' per method-signature block (always a valid composition), then merges the
#' resulting *profiles* -- never the raw fractions -- according to whichever
#' subgroups `subgroups` (already computed by the caller via
#' `multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()`) forms across those blocks.
#'
#' A subgroup formed in a later merge iteration can list an earlier
#' iteration's subgroup name as one of its own members, not just raw columns
#' -- this is unwound the same way multideconv's own (retired)
#' `expand_subgroup_members()` helper does, by repeatedly replacing any nested
#' subgroup reference with its members until only raw columns remain, then
#' merging via one flat median across all of them.
#'
#' @param counts_tpm Gene-by-sample TPM matrix.
#' @param deconv_wide Sample-by-`{method}_{signature}_{celltype}` raw fraction
#'   matrix -- `multideconv::compute.deconvolution()`'s direct output, before
#'   subgroup analysis.
#' @param subgroups The list returned by
#'   `multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis(deconv_wide)`.
#'
#' @return A gene-by-cell-type data frame of estimated expression profiles,
#'   one column per feature surviving in `subgroups[["Deconvolution matrix"]]`.
#' @keywords internal
.estimate_expression_profiles_subgroups <- function(counts_tpm, deconv_wide, subgroups) {
  block_id <- sub("^([^_]+_[^_]+)_.+$", "\\1", colnames(deconv_wide))

  profiles_by_block <- lapply(split(colnames(deconv_wide), block_id), function(cols) {
    as.matrix(.estimate_expression_profiles_samples(counts_tpm, deconv_wide[, cols, drop = FALSE]))
  })

  common_genes <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(profiles_by_block, rownames))
  all_profiles <- do.call(cbind, lapply(profiles_by_block, function(p) p[common_genes, , drop = FALSE]))

  # compute_subgroups() (called inside compute.deconvolution.analysis(), which
  # produced `subgroups`) converts its input through data.frame() internally,
  # which sanitizes column names via make.names() -- e.g. a hyphenated
  # signature name like "CBSX-HNSCC-scRNAseq" becomes "CBSX.HNSCC.scRNAseq".
  # So the Deconvolution matrix's columns and every subgroup's member names
  # already come back sanitized; all_profiles (built directly from
  # deconv_wide's raw, un-sanitized names) needs the same treatment to match.
  colnames(all_profiles) <- make.names(colnames(all_profiles))

  dt <- subgroups[["Deconvolution matrix"]]
  groups <- subgroups[["Deconvolution subgroups composition"]]

  subgroup_lookup <- list()
  for (bucket in names(groups)) {
    bucket_groups <- groups[[bucket]]
    for (subgroup_name in names(bucket_groups)) {
      subgroup_lookup[[subgroup_name]] <- bucket_groups[[subgroup_name]]
    }
  }

  expand_subgroup_members <- function(members, subgroup_map) {
    while (any(members %in% names(subgroup_map))) {
      members <- unlist(lapply(members, function(m) {
        if (m %in% names(subgroup_map)) subgroup_map[[m]] else m
      }), use.names = FALSE)
    }
    members
  }

  merged <- sapply(colnames(dt), function(feature) {
    raw_cols <- if (feature %in% names(subgroup_lookup)) {
      expand_subgroup_members(subgroup_lookup[[feature]], subgroup_lookup)
    } else if (feature %in% colnames(all_profiles)) {
      feature
    } else {
      stop("Deconvolution feature '", feature, "' could not be traced back to any ",
           "original method-signature column or subgroup -- naming mismatch between ",
           "compute.deconvolution.analysis() output and deconv_wide.")
    }
    apply(as.matrix(all_profiles[, raw_cols, drop = FALSE]), 1, stats::median)
  })
  dimnames(merged) <- list(common_genes, colnames(dt))

  stopifnot(ncol(merged) == ncol(dt))
  as.data.frame(merged)
}

#' Build RaCInG input files from raw count data
#'
#' This function combines the preprocessing and input-loading steps into a single
#' call. It generates the `L`, `R`, `C`, and `LR` CSV files from raw counts,
#' then reads them back to produce the normalised matrices and 3-D tensor required
#' by the kernel and Monte Carlo workflows.
#'
#' @param counts Gene-by-sample count matrix.
#' @param output_folder Directory where the generated `L`, `R`, `C`, and `LR` files are written.
#' @param deconv Optional patient-by-cell-type abundance matrix. If omitted, it
#'   is computed via `multideconv::compute.deconvolution()` followed by
#'   `multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()` (which identifies and
#'   collapses correlated cell-type subgroups) and
#'   `multideconv::standardize_celltype_colnames()`.
#' @param cc_network Optional ligand-receptor prior network. If omitted, it is
#'   retrieved via `liana::get_curated_omni()` (a curated, OmniPath-backed
#'   consensus of CellPhoneDB/CellChatDB/ICELLNET/connectomeDB2020/CellTalkDB)
#'   the first time this is called, then cached indefinitely as an RDS file
#'   under `tools::R_user_dir("RaCInG", "cache")` and loaded from there on every
#'   subsequent call -- avoiding a live network round-trip (and its associated
#'   transient-failure risk) on every invocation. Delete that cache file to
#'   force a refresh from OmniPath.
#' @param fun_LR Function combining a ligand's and receptor's expression
#'   values (as a length-2 vector) into one interaction strength. Default
#'   `min`: the weaker-expressed partner limits the interaction. Any function
#'   collapsing 2 values to 1 works, e.g. `prod` for the product of the two
#'   instead.
#' @param cell_expr_profile Optional gene-by-cell-type expression profile
#'   matrix. If omitted, it is estimated via per-gene non-negative least
#'   squares -- per method-signature block, then merged according to the
#'   multideconv subgroup analysis, when `deconv` is auto-computed (see
#'   `.estimate_expression_profiles_subgroups()`), or directly from the
#'   supplied `deconv` otherwise (see `.estimate_expression_profiles_samples()`).
#' @param source,target Column names to use as ligand and receptor identifiers when `cc_network` is supplied.
#' @param deconv_method Deconvolution method(s) passed to `multideconv::compute.deconvolution()`.
#' @param cbsx.name,cbsx.token Optional credentials forwarded to the deconvolution workflow.
#' @param file_name File stem used when exporting the generated CSV files.
#' @param signed Logical; if `TRUE`, also try to load a sign matrix from `output_folder`.
#'
#' @param already_normalized Logical; if `TRUE`, `counts` is treated as
#'   already TPM-normalized, **linear scale, not logged**, and the internal
#'   `ADImpute::NormalizeTPM()` gene-length/library-size normalization is
#'   skipped. Use this for datasets where only pre-normalized expression is
#'   available (e.g. public cohorts distributed as log2(TPM+1) matrices with
#'   no raw counts -- convert those back to linear scale, e.g. `2^x - 1`,
#'   before passing them here) -- applying `NormalizeTPM()` to already-
#'   normalized data would re-apply its gene-length correction on top of the
#'   original normalization, distorting relative gene expression levels.
#'   Emits a warning, since `expr_threshold` below is only meaningful if this
#'   linear-scale assumption holds -- comparing a log-scale value against it
#'   would silently apply the wrong cutoff.
#'
#' @param expr_threshold Minimum expression value, in linear-scale TPM (in
#'   `cell_expr_profile` units), a ligand or receptor must reach in its
#'   sending/receiving cell type for that ligand-receptor-celltype triple to
#'   be kept in `CC_table`.
#'
#' @return A named list with the processed input matrices and their labels:
#'   `Lmatrix`, `Rmatrix`, `Cmatrix` (normalised), `LRmatrix` (3-D tensor),
#'   `celltypes`, `ligands`, `receptors`, `Sign_matrix`, and `CC_table`.
#' @export
prepare_input_files <- function(counts, output_folder = "Results/", deconv = NULL, cc_network = NULL, fun_LR = min,
                                cell_expr_profile = NULL, source = "source_genesymbol", target = "target_genesymbol",
                                deconv_method = "Quantiseq", cbsx.name = NULL, cbsx.token = NULL, file_name = NULL,
                                signed = FALSE, already_normalized = FALSE, expr_threshold = 10){

  if (is.null(file_name)) {
    file_name <- "RaCInG_input"
  }

  .check_installed_packages(c("ADImpute", "multideconv"))
  if (already_normalized) {
    warning(
      "already_normalized = TRUE: 'counts' is assumed to already be linear-scale TPM. ",
      "expr_threshold (default ", expr_threshold, ") is compared against this scale -- ",
      "if 'counts' is actually log-transformed (e.g. log2(TPM+1)), that comparison is ",
      "wrong; convert back to linear TPM first or set expr_threshold accordingly.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
    counts.tpm <- as.matrix(counts)
  } else {
    counts.tpm <- ADImpute::NormalizeTPM(counts)
  }
  counts.log.tpm <- log2(counts.tpm + 1)

  cat("Calculating deconvolution estimates...\n")

  ## C-matrix
  # deconv_wide/subgroups stay NULL on the user-supplied-deconv path below --
  # there's no known method/signature block structure to fit expression
  # profiles per block, so that path falls back to treating the whole matrix
  # as one composition (see the expression-profile step further down).
  deconv_wide <- NULL
  subgroups <- NULL
  if (is.null(deconv)) {
    deconv_wide <- multideconv::compute.deconvolution(
      counts.tpm,
      normalized = FALSE,
      methods = deconv_method,
      credentials.mail = cbsx.name,
      credentials.token = cbsx.token,
      file_name = file_name
    )

    ## Verify patient names match between files before running the subgroup analysis
    if (!all(rownames(deconv_wide) %in% colnames(counts))) {
      stop("Patient names in deconvolution estimates do not match those in the counts matrix.")
    }

    cat("Identifying cell type subgroups...\n")
    subgroups <- multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis(deconv_wide)
    deconv <- subgroups[["Deconvolution matrix"]]
  } else {
    cat("Using provided deconvolution estimates...\n")
    if (!all(rownames(deconv) %in% colnames(counts))) {
      stop("Patient names in deconvolution estimates do not match those in the counts matrix.")
    }
  }

  ## Cell type expression profiles
  cat("\nEstimating cell type expression profiles...\n")
  if (is.null(cell_expr_profile)) {
    .check_installed_packages("nnls")
    if (!is.null(deconv_wide)) {
      # Fit one profile per method-signature block (each a valid composition),
      # then merge according to whichever subgroups multideconv formed --
      # never fit NNLS directly on the merged Deconvolution matrix (`deconv`),
      # which stitches together representatives from different blocks and is
      # not itself a valid composition. See .estimate_expression_profiles_subgroups().
      cell_expr_profile <- .estimate_expression_profiles_subgroups(counts.tpm, deconv_wide, subgroups)
    } else {
      # A user-supplied deconv has no known block structure -- treat it as one
      # composition, as before.
      cell_expr_profile <- .estimate_expression_profiles_samples(counts.tpm, deconv)
    }
  }

  ## Prior knowledge network CC
  cat("Processing cell-cell interaction network...\n")
  if (is.null(cc_network)) {
    .check_installed_packages(c("OmnipathR", "liana"))
    cache_dir <- tools::R_user_dir("RaCInG", "cache")
    cache_file <- file.path(cache_dir, "curated_omni_network.rds")
    if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
      cc_network <- readRDS(cache_file)
    } else {
      # get_curated_omni()'s underlying calls hit OmnipathR's own on-disk cache for
      # most of the network data, but at least one internal step (parameter
      # validation against OmnipathR::resources()) always makes a live request
      # regardless -- so this whole result is still subject to transient network
      # failures on every fresh R session unless cached at this level too.
      cc_network <- liana::get_curated_omni() %>%
        dplyr::filter(category_intercell_source %in% c("cell_surface_ligand", "ligand") & #check why not adhesion also or ecm
                      category_intercell_target %in% c("receptor", "adhesion")) %>%
        liana::decomplexify(columns = c("source_genesymbol", "target_genesymbol"))
      dir.create(cache_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
      saveRDS(cc_network, cache_file)
    }
  } else {
    cc_network <- cc_network %>%
      dplyr::mutate(source_genesymbol = .data[[source]], target_genesymbol = .data[[target]])
  }
  
  ## Subset expression for LR pairs (keep only interactions present in cell_expr_profile)
  keep <- integer()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(cc_network))) {
    ligand  <- cc_network$source_genesymbol[i]
    receptor <- cc_network$target_genesymbol[i]
    if (ligand %in% rownames(cell_expr_profile) & receptor %in% rownames(cell_expr_profile)) {
      keep <- c(keep, i)
    }
  }
  cc_interations_sub <- cc_network[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  
  ## Build CC table (Sender x each LR pair x Receiver)
  ## Vectorized and processed one sender at a time: the previous implementation
  ## built one data.frame per (cell_type, LR pair) via nested
  ## do.call(rbind, lapply(...)) calls, i.e. O(n_celltypes * n_LR_pairs) tiny
  ## data.frames rbound together. With many deconvolution features (e.g.
  ## combining several deconvolution methods) n_celltypes can reach 100+, and
  ## with a curated LR network of several thousand pairs this produced
  ## hundreds of thousands of rbind pieces and tens of millions of rows, slow
  ## enough (tens of minutes) and memory-heavy enough to crash on typical
  ## machines. A single vectorized pass across the full sender x LR x receiver
  ## grid fixed the speed but still peaks at O(n_celltypes^2 * n_LR_pairs)
  ## elements transiently (~15GB observed with 122 cell types, i.e. the
  ## machine's entire RAM) before the expression-threshold filter shrinks it
  ## back down. Building one sender's full receiver grid at a time and
  ## filtering immediately keeps peak memory at O(n_celltypes * n_LR_pairs)
  ## instead, independent of how many senders there are.
  celltypes_all <- colnames(cell_expr_profile)
  n_ct <- length(celltypes_all)
  n_lr <- nrow(cc_interations_sub)
  cell_expr_mat <- as.matrix(cell_expr_profile)
  L_all <- cc_interations_sub$source_genesymbol
  R_all <- cc_interations_sub$target_genesymbol
  L_row <- match(L_all, rownames(cell_expr_mat))
  R_row <- match(R_all, rownames(cell_expr_mat))

  lr_idx_rep       <- rep(seq_len(n_lr), each = n_ct)
  receiver_idx_rep <- rep(seq_len(n_ct), times = n_lr)
  R_row_rep        <- R_row[lr_idx_rep]

  ccc_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_ct), function(s) {
    Expr_Ligand   <- cell_expr_mat[L_row[lr_idx_rep], s]
    Expr_Receptor <- cell_expr_mat[cbind(R_row_rep, receiver_idx_rep)]
    keep <- Expr_Ligand >= expr_threshold & Expr_Receptor >= expr_threshold ## Keep only pairs expressed above threshold
    data.frame(
      Sender = rep(celltypes_all[s], sum(keep)),
      Ligand = L_all[lr_idx_rep[keep]],
      Expr_Ligand = Expr_Ligand[keep],
      Receiver = celltypes_all[receiver_idx_rep[keep]],
      Receptor = R_all[lr_idx_rep[keep]],
      Expr_Receptor = Expr_Receptor[keep]
    )
  }))

  ## Use the actual matched (Ligand, Receptor) pairs present in ccc_table --
  ## previously this zipped unique(Ligand) with unique(Receptor) positionally,
  ## silently mismatching real pairs whenever the two vectors had different
  ## lengths (recycling warning: "number of columns of result is not a
  ## multiple of vector length").
  lr_pairs_df <- unique(ccc_table[, c("Ligand", "Receptor")])
  ligands <- lr_pairs_df$Ligand
  receptors <- lr_pairs_df$Receptor
  LR_pairs <- paste0(ligands, "_", receptors)

  ## LR-matrix: compute fun(L, R) per sample using counts (rows=genes, cols=samples): Default min(L,R)
  cat("Computing LR matrix...\n")
  pos_lr <- match(c(rbind(ligands, receptors)), rownames(counts.log.tpm))
  pos_lr <- matrix(pos_lr, nrow = 2)
  
  LR_matrix <- apply(pos_lr, 2, function(idx) {
    if (any(is.na(idx))) {
      return(rep(NA, ncol(counts.log.tpm)))
    }
    apply(counts.log.tpm[idx, , drop = FALSE], 2, function(x) fun_LR(x))
  })
  colnames(LR_matrix) <- LR_pairs
  rownames(LR_matrix) <- gsub(".", "-", rownames(LR_matrix), fixed = TRUE)
  
  ## L-matrix: ligands vs cell types compatibility (from filtered cc table) ## how do you know which ligand is expressed in which cell type? there is no database?
  cat("Computing L-matrix...\n")
  celltypes <- unique(ccc_table$Sender)
  ligs <- unique(ccc_table$Ligand)
  Lmatrix <- matrix(0, nrow = length(celltypes), ncol = length(ligs),
                    dimnames = list(celltypes, ligs))
  for (ct in celltypes) {
    tmp <- ccc_table %>% dplyr::filter(Sender == ct) %>% dplyr::select(Ligand) %>% unique()
    Lmatrix[ct, tmp$Ligand] <- 1
  }
  
  ## R-matrix: receptors vs cell types compatibility
  cat("Computing R-matrix...\n")
  recs <- unique(ccc_table$Receptor)
  Rmatrix <- matrix(0, nrow = length(celltypes), ncol = length(recs),
                    dimnames = list(celltypes, recs))
  for (ct in celltypes) {
    tmp <- ccc_table %>% dplyr::filter(Receiver == ct) %>% dplyr::select(Receptor) %>% unique()
    Rmatrix[ct, tmp$Receptor] <- 1
  }
  
  ## Output files
  cat("Exporting input files for RaCiNG...\n")
  if (!dir.exists(output_folder)) dir.create(output_folder, recursive = TRUE)
  utils::write.csv(Lmatrix, file.path(output_folder, paste0("Lmatrix_", file_name, ".csv")))
  utils::write.csv(Rmatrix, file.path(output_folder, paste0("Rmatrix_", file_name, ".csv")))
  utils::write.csv(deconv, file.path(output_folder, paste0("Cmatrix_", file_name, ".csv")))
  utils::write.csv(LR_matrix, file.path(output_folder, paste0("LRmatrix_", file_name, ".csv")))
  utils::write.csv(ccc_table, file.path(output_folder, paste0("CC_table_", file_name, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
  
  cat("Input files generated and saved to:", output_folder, "\n")

  ## Read the written CSVs back through generateInput to obtain the

  ## normalised matrices and 3-D tensor expected by downstream functions.
  cat("Processing input matrices...\n")
  processed <- generateInput(file_name, output_folder = output_folder,
                             read_signs = signed)

  ## Append the CC table to the processed result
  processed$CC_table <- ccc_table

  return(processed)
}

1	#' Compute the RaCInG kernel for one or more patients
2	#'
3	#' The kernel is the *unweighted* structural kernel: cell-type abundances are
4	#' not baked into it. `calculateDirect()`, `calculateWedges()`,
5	#' `computeTriangles()`, and `computeGSCC()` each multiply in the abundance of
6	#' every node they use, exactly once per node, when computing raw
7	#' (unnormalized) features from this kernel.
8	#'
9	#' @param liglist Cell-by-ligand compatibility matrix.
10	#' @param reclist Cell-by-receptor compatibility matrix.
11	#' @param Cmatrix Patient-by-cell-type abundance matrix.
12	#' @param LRmatrix Ligand-by-receptor-by-patient interaction tensor.
13	#' @param normalize Logical; if `TRUE`, also compute a second kernel
14	#'   (`kernel_norm`) under a NULL DISTRIBUTION where every ligand-receptor
15	#'   pair that is structurally possible (nonzero in `LRmatrix`) is given the
16	#'   same uniform strength (`1 / number of active pairs for that patient`),
17	#'   instead of its real measured expression-derived strength. `kernel_norm`
18	#'   therefore reflects only network topology and cell-type abundance --
19	#'   "how much communication would you expect between these two cell types if
20	#'   every possible ligand-receptor pair were equally active" -- with no
21	#'   information about which pairs are actually more or less expressed.
22	#'   Downstream functions (`calculateDirect()`, `calculateWedges()`, etc.) use
23	#'   this as a baseline to compute a composition-independent enrichment score
24	#'   (`kernel / kernel_norm`) instead of the raw, abundance-weighted score --
25	#'   the abundance weighting cancels out of that ratio algebraically, since
26	#'   both `kernel` and `kernel_norm` are built from the same per-patient
27	#'   `lig_weight`/`rec_weight` terms. Use `normalize = FALSE` (default) when
28	#'   you want absolute communication strength (abundance and real LR
29	#'   expression both matter); use `normalize = TRUE` when you want a score
30	#'   that isolates specificity/enrichment of a cell-type pair's communication
31	#'   relative to what topology alone would predict, independent of how common
32	#'   those cell types are or how strong LR expression is overall.
33	#'
34	#' @return Either a 3D kernel array `[sender x receiver x patient]`, or (when
35	#'   `normalize = TRUE`) a list with `kernel` and `kernel_norm`.
36	#' @export
37	compute_kernel <- function(liglist, reclist, Cmatrix, LRmatrix, normalize = FALSE) {
38	  # liglist:   [cell type × ligand] binary/weighted matrix mapping cell types to ligands
39	  # reclist:   [cell type × receptor] binary/weighted matrix mapping cell types to receptors
40	  # Cmatrix:   [patient × cell type] cell type abundances for each patient
41	  # LRmatrix:  [ligand × receptor × patient] ligand-receptor interaction strengths for each patient
42	  # normalize: if TRUE, also compute the kernel under a uniformized (null-distribution) LRmatrix --
43	  #            see @param normalize above for what this represents and why you'd want it.
44	  #
45	  # Return:
46	  #  - if normalize == FALSE: kernel array [sender x receiver x patient]
47	  #  - if normalize == TRUE: list(kernel = kernel, kernel_norm = normalized_kernel)
48	  #
49	  # NOTE: the returned kernel is the *unweighted* structural kernel (cell-type
50	  # abundances are NOT baked in). Each feature-extraction function multiplies
51	  # in the abundance of every node it uses, exactly once per node, mirroring
52	  # the original Python implementation.
53	
54	  # Ensure matrix format
55	  Cmatrix <- if (is.null(dim(Cmatrix))) matrix(Cmatrix, nrow = 1) else Cmatrix
56	  n_patients <- nrow(Cmatrix)
57	  n_celltypes <- ncol(Cmatrix)
58	
59	  # Prepare normalized LRmatrix copy if requested (do not overwrite original LRmatrix)
60	  if (normalize) {
61	    LRmatrix_norm <- LRmatrix
62	    normvec <- 1 / apply(LRmatrix_norm > 0, 3, sum)  # inverse of positive interactions per patient
63	    for (p in 1:n_patients) {
64	      copy <- LRmatrix_norm[, , p]
65	      copy[copy > 0] <- normvec[p]           # scale positive interactions
66	      LRmatrix_norm[, , p] <- copy
67	    }
68	  }
69	
70	  # Output: [sender x receiver x patient]
71	  kernel <- array(0, dim = c(n_celltypes, n_celltypes, n_patients))
72	  if (normalize) kernel_norm <- array(0, dim = c(n_celltypes, n_celltypes, n_patients))
73	
74	  for (p in 1:n_patients) {
75	
76	    Cvec <- Cmatrix[p, ]  # cell abundances
77	
78	    # ---- ligand weights ----
79	    # weightlig[i] = total abundance-weighted ligand i expression across cell types
80	    lig_norm <- colSums(sweep(liglist, 1, Cvec, "*"))
81	    lig_norm[lig_norm == 0] <- 1  # avoid division by zero
82	    # lig_weight[A, i] = P(ligand i is sent by cell type A)
83	    lig_weight <- sweep(liglist, 2, lig_norm, "/")
84	
85	    # ---- receptor weights ----
86	    rec_norm <- colSums(sweep(reclist, 1, Cvec, "*"))
87	    rec_norm[rec_norm == 0] <- 1
88	    # rec_weight[B, j] = P(receptor j is received by cell type B)
89	    rec_weight <- sweep(reclist, 2, rec_norm, "/")
90	
91	    # ---- aggregate over ligand-receptor pairs ----
92	    # kernel[A, B] = sum over (i,j) of P(A sends i) * LRmatrix[i,j] * P(B receives j)
93	    kernel[, , p] <- lig_weight %*% LRmatrix[, , p] %*% t(rec_weight)
94	
95	    if (normalize) {
96	      kernel_norm[, , p] <- lig_weight %*% LRmatrix_norm[, , p] %*% t(rec_weight)
97	    }
98	  }
99	
100	  if (normalize) {
101	    return(list(kernel = kernel, kernel_norm = kernel_norm))
102	  } else {
103	    return(kernel)
104	  }
105	}
106	
107	#' Calculate direct communication features from a kernel
108	#'
109	#' @param kernel Kernel array returned by [compute_kernel()].
110	#' @param unifKernel Optional normalized baseline kernel.
111	#' @param cells Character vector of cell-type names.
112	#' @param Dcell Patient-by-cell-type abundance matrix, used to weight raw
113	#'   (unnormalized) scores. Ignored when `unifKernel` is supplied, since the
114	#'   abundance weights cancel out of the ratio.
115	#' @param bundle Logical; if `TRUE`, combine reciprocal directions.
116	#' @param patient_names Optional character vector of patient labels, matching
117	#'   the patient order in `kernel`. Defaults to `Patient_1`, `Patient_2`, ...
118	#'   when omitted, matching [compute_racing_montecarlo()]'s output when it
119	#'   is also given real names.
120	#' @param zero_threshold Drop a cell-type pair once its fraction of
121	#'   zero-valued patients reaches this threshold. Default `1` only drops
122	#'   pairs that are zero for every patient (the original behavior); lower it
123	#'   (e.g. `0.9`) to also drop merely zero-inflated pairs.
124	#'
125	#' @return A patient-by-feature data frame of direct communication scores.
126	#'   Cell-type pairs with no possible ligand-receptor pathway in any patient
127	#'   (zero for every patient) are dropped rather than returned as all-zero
128	#'   columns.
129	#' @export
130	calculateDirect <- function(kernel, unifKernel = NULL, cells, Dcell = NULL, bundle = TRUE, patient_names = NULL, zero_threshold = 1) {
131	  n_celltypes <- length(cells)      # number of cell types
132	  n_patients <- dim(kernel)[3]      # number of patients
133	
134	  df_list <- list()                 # list to store each column before converting to data frame
135	
136	  # Loop over all cell type pairs (sender i, receiver j).
137	  # If bundle = TRUE, only the upper triangle is used to avoid double counting.
138	  for (i in 1:n_celltypes) {
139	    for (j in if (bundle) i:n_celltypes else 1:n_celltypes) {
140	
141	      colname <- paste0("Dir_", cells[i], "_", cells[j])
142	
143	      if (!is.null(unifKernel)) {
144	        # normalized direct score: abundance weights cancel out of the ratio
145	        value <- if (bundle) {
146	          (kernel[i, j, ] + kernel[j, i, ]) / (unifKernel[i, j, ] + unifKernel[j, i, ])
147	        } else {
148	          kernel[i, j, ] / unifKernel[i, j, ]
149	        }
150	        value[is.nan(value)] <- 0 # no possible ligand-receptor pathway between i and j (0/0): no communication, not undefined
151	      } else {
152	        # raw direct score: weight explicitly by the abundance of each node
153	        value <- if (bundle) {
154	          Dcell[, i] * Dcell[, j] * (kernel[i, j, ] + kernel[j, i, ])
155	        } else {
156	          Dcell[, i] * Dcell[, j] * kernel[i, j, ]
157	        }
158	      }
159	
160	      df_list[[colname]] <- value   # add the vector of patient scores as a new column
161	    }
162	  }
163	
164	  df <- as.data.frame(df_list)
165	  rownames(df) <- if (!is.null(patient_names)) patient_names else paste0("Patient_", 1:n_patients)
166	
167	  # Drop cell-type pairs whose fraction of zero-valued patients reaches
168	  # zero_threshold -- default 1 keeps only the original behavior (drop a pair
169	  # only if it's zero for every single patient, a structurally-impossible
170	  # pathway; both branches above fill the impossible NaN case with 0, so this
171	  # is a correct and sufficient test regardless of raw vs normalized). Lower
172	  # zero_threshold (e.g. 0.9) to also drop merely zero-inflated pairs, which
173	  # this all-zero check alone does not catch.
174	  df <- df[, colMeans(df == 0) < zero_threshold, drop = FALSE]
175	
176	  return(df)
177	}
178	
179	#' Calculate wedge features from a kernel
180	#'
181	#' @param kernel Kernel array returned by [compute_kernel()].
182	#' @param unifKernel Optional normalized baseline kernel.
183	#' @param cells Character vector of cell-type names.
184	#' @param Dcell Patient-by-cell-type abundance matrix, used to weight raw
185	#'   (unnormalized) scores. Ignored when `unifKernel` is supplied.
186	#' @param bundle Logical; if `TRUE`, combine directionally equivalent wedges.
187	#' @param patient_names Optional character vector of patient labels, matching
188	#'   the patient order in `kernel`. Defaults to `Patient_1`, `Patient_2`, ...
189	#'   when omitted.
190	#' @param zero_threshold Drop a wedge once its fraction of zero-valued
191	#'   patients reaches this threshold. Default `1` only drops wedges that are
192	#'   zero for every patient (the original behavior); lower it (e.g. `0.9`) to
193	#'   also drop merely zero-inflated wedges.
194	#'
195	#' @return A patient-by-feature data frame of wedge scores. Triplets with no
196	#'   possible ligand-receptor pathway in any patient (zero for every
197	#'   patient) are dropped rather than returned as all-zero columns.
198	#' @export
199	calculateWedges <- function(kernel, unifKernel = NULL, cells, Dcell = NULL, bundle = TRUE, patient_names = NULL, zero_threshold = 1) {
200	  n_celltypes <- length(cells)
201	  n_patients <- dim(kernel)[3]
202	
203	  # Build the full (i, j, k) index grid vectorized, up front, instead of a
204	  # triple nested for-loop with a per-triplet df_list[[colname]] <- value
205	  # assignment -- that pattern grows an R named list one entry at a time,
206	  # which for realistic cell-type counts (e.g. 106) means n^2*(n+1)/2 (~600K,
207	  # bundled) or n^3 (~1.2M, unbundled) individual list insertions plus a
208	  # final as.data.frame() on all of them: this was the actual crash/hang,
209	  # not the underlying arithmetic. A single vectorized computation over the
210	  # whole grid does the same math with none of that per-element overhead
211	  # (mirrors the fix already applied to compute_results_processing() on the
212	  # Monte Carlo side for the same O(n^3) list-growth pattern).
213	  if (bundle) {
214	    grid <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_celltypes), function(jj) {
215	      expand.grid(i = seq_len(n_celltypes), j = jj, k = jj:n_celltypes)
216	    }))
217	  } else {
218	    grid <- expand.grid(i = seq_len(n_celltypes), j = seq_len(n_celltypes), k = seq_len(n_celltypes))
219	  }
220	  i <- grid$i; j <- grid$j; k <- grid$k
221	
222	  # Flatten kernel's [sender, receiver, patient] array to [(sender*receiver), patient]
223	  # so kernel[a, b, ] for every (a, b) pair in the grid can be pulled out in
224	  # one indexed lookup per patient column, instead of one R-level `kernel[i,j,]`
225	  # subset per triplet.
226	  kernel_mat <- matrix(kernel, nrow = n_celltypes * n_celltypes, ncol = n_patients)
227	  idx2 <- function(a, b) a + (b - 1L) * n_celltypes
228	  Kij <- kernel_mat[idx2(i, j), , drop = FALSE]
229	  Kjk <- kernel_mat[idx2(j, k), , drop = FALSE]
230	  if (bundle) {
231	    Kkj0 <- kernel_mat[idx2(k, j), , drop = FALSE]
232	    Kji0 <- kernel_mat[idx2(j, i), , drop = FALSE]
233	    struct_core <- Kij * Kjk + Kkj0 * Kji0
234	  } else {
235	    struct_core <- Kij * Kjk
236	  }
237	
238	  # Drop triplets with no possible ligand-receptor pathway in any patient
239	  # (zero structural kernel product for every patient) before doing any
240	  # further (abundance-weighting or ratio) computation on them -- unifKernel
241	  # is a rescaling of the same nonzero pattern as kernel (normalization only
242	  # rescales already-positive entries, see compute_kernel()), so checking
243	  # kernel's pattern alone is correct and sufficient for both raw and
244	  # normalized output. This both shrinks the returned feature count and cuts
245	  # the working-set size for the (possibly very large, e.g. ~600K rows at
246	  # 106 cell types) computation below.
247	  possible <- rowSums(struct_core != 0) > 0
248	  if (!all(possible)) {
249	    i <- i[possible]; j <- j[possible]; k <- k[possible]
250	    Kij <- Kij[possible, , drop = FALSE]
251	    Kjk <- Kjk[possible, , drop = FALSE]
252	    if (bundle) { Kkj0 <- Kkj0[possible, , drop = FALSE]; Kji0 <- Kji0[possible, , drop = FALSE] }
253	  }
254	  rm(struct_core)
255	
256	  if (!is.null(unifKernel)) {
257	    unif_mat <- matrix(unifKernel, nrow = n_celltypes * n_celltypes, ncol = n_patients)
258	    UKij <- unif_mat[idx2(i, j), , drop = FALSE]
259	    UKjk <- unif_mat[idx2(j, k), , drop = FALSE]
260	
261	    if (bundle) {
262	      UKkj <- unif_mat[idx2(k, j), , drop = FALSE]
263	      UKji <- unif_mat[idx2(j, i), , drop = FALSE]
264	      num <- Kij * Kjk + Kkj0 * Kji0
265	      den <- UKij * UKjk + UKkj * UKji
266	    } else {
267	      num <- Kij * Kjk
268	      den <- UKij * UKjk
269	    }
270	    value <- num / den
271	    value[is.nan(value)] <- 0 # no possible ligand-receptor pathway through this triplet (0/0): no communication, not undefined
272	  } else {
273	    # Weight by abundance per patient via a small per-patient loop
274	    # (n_patients is typically <=~150) rather than materializing three
275	    # separate full [n_combo x n_patients] copies of Dcell (Di, Dj, Dk) --
276	    # for n_combo in the hundreds of thousands to over a million (large
277	    # cell-type counts), those three extra full-size matrices were the
278	    # single biggest avoidable memory cost in this function; Dmat[p, i] for
279	    # one patient p is just a cheap n_combo-length index/recycle, not a copy.
280	    Dmat <- as.matrix(Dcell)  # [n_patients x n_celltypes]
281	    core <- if (bundle) Kij * Kjk + Kkj0 * Kji0 else Kij * Kjk
282	    value <- core
283	    for (p in seq_len(n_patients)) {
284	      value[, p] <- Dmat[p, i] * Dmat[p, j] * Dmat[p, k] * core[, p]
285	    }
286	  }
287	
288	  out <- t(value)  # [n_patients x n_combo]
289	  colnames(out) <- paste0("W_", cells[i], "_", cells[j], "_", cells[k])
290	  df <- as.data.frame(out)
291	  rownames(df) <- if (!is.null(patient_names)) patient_names else paste0("Patient_", 1:n_patients)
292	
293	  # The structural pre-filter above only removes wedges with zero kernel
294	  # product for every patient (checked before abundance-weighting); it does
295	  # not catch wedges whose final, abundance-weighted values are merely
296	  # zero-inflated (or become all-zero only after weighting, e.g. a cell type
297	  # with zero abundance in every patient). This final check catches both,
298	  # controlled the same way as calculateDirect()'s zero_threshold: default 1
299	  # keeps only the original all-zero-drop behavior.
300	  df <- df[, colMeans(df == 0) < zero_threshold, drop = FALSE]
301	
302	  return(df)
303	}

324	#' Compute GSCC features from kernel matrices
325	#'
326	#' @param kernel Kernel array from [compute_kernel()].
327	#' @param Dcell Patient-by-cell-type abundance matrix.
328	#' @param cell_names Character vector of cell-type labels.
329	#' @param patient_names Character vector of patient names.
330	#' @param unifKernel Optional normalized baseline kernel.
331	#' @param norm Logical; if `TRUE`, divide by the baseline GSCC values.
332	#' @param lab Scaling factor for interaction strengths.
333	#'
334	#' @return A data frame with GSCC feature values per patient.
335	#' @export
336	computeGSCC <- function(kernel, Dcell, cell_names, patient_names,
337	                        unifKernel = NULL, norm = FALSE, lab = 1) {
338	  # kernel: [sender x receiver x patient] matrix from compute_kernel
339	  # Dcell: [patient x cell type] cell abundances (can be used to scale if needed)
340	  # cell_names: vector of cell type names
341	  # patient_names: vector of patient names
342	  # unifKernel: optional uniform kernel (same dimensions as kernel) for normalization
343	  # norm: boolean, whether to normalize by uniform kernel
344	  # lab: scaling factor for interaction strengths
345	
346	  n_patients <- nrow(Dcell)
347	  n_cells <- length(cell_names)
348	
349	  # Matrices to store GSCC per patient and per cell type
350	  GSCCsizes <- matrix(0, nrow = n_patients, ncol = n_cells + 1)  # last column = total GSCC
351	  GSCCsizesN <- if (!is.null(unifKernel)) matrix(0, nrow = n_patients, ncol = n_cells + 1) else NULL
352	
353	  # Loop over patients
354	  for (p in 1:n_patients) {
355	    q <- Dcell[p, ]  # cell abundances vector for this patient
356	
357	    # Construct mu matrices for Poisson branching process
358	    muP <- matrix(0, nrow = n_cells, ncol = n_cells)
359	    muM <- matrix(0, nrow = n_cells, ncol = n_cells)
360	    for (i in 1:n_cells) {
361	      for (j in 1:n_cells) {
362	        muP[i, j] <- lab * kernel[j, i, p] * q[j]  # incoming contribution
363	        muM[i, j] <- lab * kernel[i, j, p] * q[j]  # outgoing contribution
364	      }
365	    }
366	
367	    # Solve the branching process equations using nleqslv
368	    solP <- nleqslv::nleqslv(rep(1, n_cells), poiBPFunc, M = muP, sens = n_cells)
369	    solM <- nleqslv::nleqslv(rep(1, n_cells), poiBPFunc, M = muM, sens = n_cells)
370	
371	    x <- solP$x
372	    y <- solM$x
373	
374	    # GSCC per cell type and total
375	    GSCCsizes[p, 1:n_cells] <- x * y * q
376	    GSCCsizes[p, n_cells + 1] <- sum(x * y * q)
377	
378	    # If uniform kernel is provided, calculate same for normalization
379	    if (!is.null(unifKernel)) {
380	      muP_N <- matrix(0, nrow = n_cells, ncol = n_cells)
381	      muM_N <- matrix(0, nrow = n_cells, ncol = n_cells)
382	      for (i in 1:n_cells) {
383	        for (j in 1:n_cells) {
384	          muP_N[i, j] <- lab * unifKernel[j, i, p] * q[j]
385	          muM_N[i, j] <- lab * unifKernel[i, j, p] * q[j]
386	        }
387	      }
388	      solP_N <- nleqslv::nleqslv(rep(1, n_cells), poiBPFunc, M = muP_N, sens = n_cells)
389	      solM_N <- nleqslv::nleqslv(rep(1, n_cells), poiBPFunc, M = muM_N, sens = n_cells)
390	      xN <- solP_N$x
391	      yN <- solM_N$x
392	      GSCCsizesN[p, 1:n_cells] <- xN * yN * q
393	      GSCCsizesN[p, n_cells + 1] <- sum(xN * yN * q)
394	    }
395	  }
396	
397	  # Normalize by uniform kernel if requested
398	  if (norm && !is.null(unifKernel)) {
399	    normvals <- GSCCsizes / GSCCsizesN
400	    normvals[is.nan(normvals)] <- 1  # handle division by zero
401	    df <- as.data.frame(normvals)
402	  } else {
403	    df <- as.data.frame(GSCCsizes)
404	  }
405	
406	  # Set column and row names
407	  colnames(df) <- c(paste0("GSCC_", cell_names), "GSCC_total")
408	  rownames(df) <- patient_names
409	
410	  return(df)
411	}

413	#' Compute triangle features from kernel matrices
414	#'
415	#' @param kernel Kernel array from [compute_kernel()].
416	#' @param cell_names Character vector of cell-type names.
417	#' @param patient_names Character vector of patient names.
418	#' @param Dcell Patient-by-cell-type abundance matrix, used to weight raw
419	#'   (unnormalized) scores. Ignored when `unifKernel`/`norm` is used.
420	#' @param unifKernel Optional normalized baseline kernel.
421	#' @param norm Logical; if `TRUE`, divide by the baseline triangle scores.
422	#' @param bundle Logical; if `TRUE`, aggregate all directions into a single
423	#'   "Tr" triangle score per triple. If `FALSE`, two scores are returned per
424	#'   triple: "TT" (trust/transitive triangle, `i->j->k` and `i->k`) and,
425	#'   for `i<=j<=k` only, "CT" (cycle triangle, `i->j->k->i`).
426	#' @param zero_threshold Drop a triangle once its fraction of zero-valued
427	#'   patients reaches this threshold. Default `1` only drops triangles that
428	#'   are zero for every patient (the original behavior); lower it (e.g.
429	#'   `0.9`) to also drop merely zero-inflated triangles.
430	#'
431	#' @return A patient-by-feature data frame of triangle scores. Triples with
432	#'   no possible ligand-receptor pathway in any patient (zero for every
433	#'   patient) are dropped rather than returned as all-zero columns.
434	#' @export
435	computeTriangles <- function(kernel, cell_names, patient_names, Dcell = NULL,
436	                             unifKernel = NULL, norm = FALSE, bundle = TRUE, zero_threshold = 1) {
437	  n_patients <- dim(kernel)[3]   # number of patients
438	  n_cells <- length(cell_names)   # number of cell types
439	
440	  # Build the (i, j, k) index grid(s) vectorized, up front, instead of a
441	  # triple nested for-loop with a per-triple df_list[[colname]] <- value
442	  # assignment -- for realistic cell-type counts this pattern reaches
443	  # n(n+1)(n+2)/6 (bundled) or a full n^3 (unbundled -- what "TT" always
444	  # requests via compute_kernel_features()) individual list insertions, which
445	  # was the actual crash/hang for larger cohorts (e.g. n=106 gives ~1.2M
446	  # triples), not the underlying arithmetic. See the equivalent fix in
447	  # calculateWedges() for the same pattern.
448	  kernel_mat <- matrix(kernel, nrow = n_cells * n_cells, ncol = n_patients)
449	  unif_mat <- if (!is.null(unifKernel)) matrix(unifKernel, nrow = n_cells * n_cells, ncol = n_patients) else NULL
450	  idx2 <- function(a, b) a + (b - 1L) * n_cells
451	  get_val <- function(mat, a, b) mat[idx2(a, b), , drop = FALSE]
452	
453	  # Weight by abundance per patient via a small per-patient loop
454	  # (n_patients is typically <=~150) rather than materializing three
455	  # separate full [n_combo x n_patients] copies of Dcell (Di, Dj, Dk) --
456	  # for n_combo in the hundreds of thousands to over a million (large
457	  # cell-type counts), those three extra full-size matrices were the
458	  # single biggest avoidable memory cost in this function; Dmat[p, idx] for
459	  # one patient p is just a cheap n_combo-length index/recycle, not a copy.
460	  weight_or_ratio_vec <- function(num_mat, den_mat, i_idx, j_idx, k_idx) {
461	    if (norm && !is.null(unifKernel)) {
462	      value <- num_mat / den_mat
463	      value[is.nan(value)] <- 1
464	      value
465	    } else {
466	      Dmat <- as.matrix(Dcell)
467	      value <- num_mat
468	      for (p in seq_len(n_patients)) {
469	        value[, p] <- Dmat[p, i_idx] * Dmat[p, j_idx] * Dmat[p, k_idx] * num_mat[, p]
470	      }
471	      value
472	    }
473	  }
474	
475	  if (bundle) {
476	    grid <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_cells), function(ii) {
477	      do.call(rbind, lapply(ii:n_cells, function(jj) {
478	        expand.grid(i = ii, j = jj, k = jj:n_cells)
479	      }))
480	    }))
481	    i <- grid$i; j <- grid$j; k <- grid$k
482	
483	    # Sum all 8 edge-direction combinations of the 3 undirected edges
484	    # (2 cyclic + 6 transitive) to remove directionality entirely.
485	    Kij <- get_val(kernel_mat, i, j); Kjk <- get_val(kernel_mat, j, k); Kki <- get_val(kernel_mat, k, i)
486	    Kik <- get_val(kernel_mat, i, k); Kkj <- get_val(kernel_mat, k, j); Kji <- get_val(kernel_mat, j, i)
487	    num <- Kij*Kjk*Kki + Kij*Kjk*Kik + Kij*Kkj*Kik + Kij*Kkj*Kki +
488	           Kji*Kkj*Kki + Kji*Kjk*Kki + Kji*Kjk*Kik + Kji*Kkj*Kik
489	
490	    # Drop triples with no possible ligand-receptor pathway in any patient
491	    # (zero structural kernel product for every patient), before the
492	    # (possibly ratio or abundance-weighting) computation below -- unifKernel
493	    # shares kernel's nonzero pattern (see calculateWedges() for why), so
494	    # checking the raw structural product alone is correct here too.
495	    possible <- rowSums(num != 0) > 0
496	    if (!all(possible)) {
497	      i <- i[possible]; j <- j[possible]; k <- k[possible]
498	      Kij <- Kij[possible,,drop=FALSE]; Kjk <- Kjk[possible,,drop=FALSE]; Kki <- Kki[possible,,drop=FALSE]
499	      Kik <- Kik[possible,,drop=FALSE]; Kkj <- Kkj[possible,,drop=FALSE]; Kji <- Kji[possible,,drop=FALSE]
500	      num <- num[possible,,drop=FALSE]
501	    }
502	
503	    den <- NULL
504	    if (norm && !is.null(unifKernel)) {
505	      UKij <- get_val(unif_mat, i, j); UKjk <- get_val(unif_mat, j, k); UKki <- get_val(unif_mat, k, i)
506	      UKik <- get_val(unif_mat, i, k); UKkj <- get_val(unif_mat, k, j); UKji <- get_val(unif_mat, j, i)
507	      den <- UKij*UKjk*UKki + UKij*UKjk*UKik + UKij*UKkj*UKik + UKij*UKkj*UKki +
508	             UKji*UKkj*UKki + UKji*UKjk*UKki + UKji*UKjk*UKik + UKji*UKkj*UKik
509	    }
510	
511	    value <- weight_or_ratio_vec(num, den, i, j, k)
512	    out <- t(value)
513	    colnames(out) <- paste0("Tr_", cell_names[i], "_", cell_names[j], "_", cell_names[k])
514	
515	  } else {
516	    grid <- expand.grid(i = seq_len(n_cells), j = seq_len(n_cells), k = seq_len(n_cells))
517	    i_full <- grid$i; j_full <- grid$j; k_full <- grid$k
518	
519	    # Kij/Kjk (and their unifKernel counterparts) are shared by both TT and
520	    # CT below, so computed once and reused; Kik/Kki are each used by only
521	    # one of the two and freed (rm + gc) right after, since at up to ~1.2M
522	    # combinations x n_patients each of these full-size matrices is itself a
523	    # substantial allocation.
524	    Kij <- get_val(kernel_mat, i_full, j_full)
525	    Kjk <- get_val(kernel_mat, j_full, k_full)
526	    UKij <- if (norm && !is.null(unifKernel)) get_val(unif_mat, i_full, j_full) else NULL
527	    UKjk <- if (norm && !is.null(unifKernel)) get_val(unif_mat, j_full, k_full) else NULL
528	
529	    # --- Trust triangle (transitive): i->j, j->k, i->k -- every (i,j,k) triple ---
530	    Kik <- get_val(kernel_mat, i_full, k_full)
531	    num_tt <- Kij * Kjk * Kik
532	    rm(Kik)
533	
534	    # Drop triples with no possible pathway in any patient (zero structural
535	    # kernel product for every patient), before the (possibly ratio or
536	    # abundance-weighting) computation -- unifKernel shares kernel's nonzero
537	    # pattern (see calculateWedges()), so checking the raw structural
538	    # product alone is correct here too.
539	    possible_tt <- rowSums(num_tt != 0) > 0
540	    i_tt <- i_full[possible_tt]; j_tt <- j_full[possible_tt]; k_tt <- k_full[possible_tt]
541	    num_tt <- num_tt[possible_tt, , drop = FALSE]
542	    den_tt <- if (norm && !is.null(unifKernel)) {
543	      (UKij * UKjk * get_val(unif_mat, i_full, k_full))[possible_tt, , drop = FALSE]
544	    } else NULL
545	    value_tt <- weight_or_ratio_vec(num_tt, den_tt, i_tt, j_tt, k_tt)
546	    rm(num_tt, den_tt); gc(FALSE)
547	    colnames_tt <- paste0("TT_", cell_names[i_tt], "_", cell_names[j_tt], "_", cell_names[k_tt])
548	
549	    # --- Cycle triangle: i->j->k->i (only counted once per unordered triple, i<=j<=k) ---
550	    keep_ct <- i_full <= j_full & j_full <= k_full
551	    i_ct0 <- i_full[keep_ct]; j_ct0 <- j_full[keep_ct]; k_ct0 <- k_full[keep_ct]
552	    Kki <- get_val(kernel_mat, k_full, i_full)
553	    num_ct <- (Kij * Kjk * Kki)[keep_ct, , drop = FALSE]
554	    den_ct_full <- if (norm && !is.null(unifKernel)) {
555	      (UKij * UKjk * get_val(unif_mat, k_full, i_full))[keep_ct, , drop = FALSE]
556	    } else NULL
557	    rm(Kki, Kij, Kjk, UKij, UKjk)
558	
559	    possible_ct <- rowSums(num_ct != 0) > 0
560	    i_ct <- i_ct0[possible_ct]; j_ct <- j_ct0[possible_ct]; k_ct <- k_ct0[possible_ct]
561	    num_ct <- num_ct[possible_ct, , drop = FALSE]
562	    den_ct <- if (!is.null(den_ct_full)) den_ct_full[possible_ct, , drop = FALSE] else NULL
563	    value_ct <- weight_or_ratio_vec(num_ct, den_ct, i_ct, j_ct, k_ct)
564	    rm(num_ct, den_ct); gc(FALSE)
565	    colnames_ct <- paste0("CT_", cell_names[i_ct], "_", cell_names[j_ct], "_", cell_names[k_ct])
566	
567	    out <- t(rbind(value_tt, value_ct))
568	    colnames(out) <- c(colnames_tt, colnames_ct)
569	  }
570	
571	  # Convert to a dataframe: rows = patients, columns = triangles
572	  df <- as.data.frame(out)
573	  rownames(df) <- patient_names
574	
575	  # The structural pre-filters above (`possible`/`possible_tt`/`possible_ct`)
576	  # only remove triangles with zero kernel product for every patient, checked
577	  # before abundance-weighting; they don't catch triangles whose final,
578	  # abundance-weighted values are merely zero-inflated (or become all-zero
579	  # only after weighting, e.g. a cell type with zero abundance in every
580	  # patient). This final check catches both, controlled the same way as
581	  # calculateDirect()/calculateWedges()'s zero_threshold: default 1 keeps
582	  # only the original all-zero-drop behavior.
583	  df <- df[, colMeans(df == 0) < zero_threshold, drop = FALSE]
584	
585	  return(df)
586	}

588	#' Derive communication features from a kernel
589	#'
590	#' @param kernel Kernel array from [compute_kernel()].
591	#' @param unifKernel Optional normalized baseline kernel.
592	#' @param celltypes Character vector of cell-type labels.
593	#' @param communication_type Feature family to compute (`"D"`, `"W"`, `"TT"`,
594	#'   or `"GSCC"`; `"TT"` returns both trust- and cycle-triangle columns
595	#'   together, see [computeTriangles()]), or a character vector of several of
596	#'   these. Since the kernel itself (`kernel`/`unifKernel`) is passed in
597	#'   already computed, requesting multiple types here costs nothing extra to
598	#'   compute per type beyond that one kernel -- no re-derivation happens for
599	#'   any of them. With more than one type, the return value is a named list
600	#'   (one data frame per type) instead of a single data frame.
601	#' @param bundle Logical; if `TRUE`, merge directionally equivalent features where appropriate.
602	#' @param patient_names Optional patient labels.
603	#' @param Dcell Patient-by-cell-type abundance matrix. Always required for
604	#'   `"GSCC"`; required for `"D"`, `"W"`, `"TT"` only when `unifKernel` is not
605	#'   supplied (raw, unnormalized features).
606	#' @param norm Logical; if `TRUE`, compute normalized features when a baseline is supplied.
607	#' @param patient_idx Optional patient index subset.
608	#' @param zero_threshold Drop a feature once its fraction of zero-valued
609	#'   patients reaches this threshold. Default `1` only drops features that
610	#'   are zero for every patient (the original behavior); lower it (e.g.
611	#'   `0.9`) to also drop merely zero-inflated features. Passed through to
612	#'   [calculateDirect()]/[calculateWedges()]/[computeTriangles()]; ignored for `"GSCC"`.
613	#'
614	#' @return A data frame of feature values for the selected patients, or (when
615	#'   `communication_type` has more than one entry) a named list of such data
616	#'   frames, one per requested type.
617	#' @export
618	compute_kernel_features <- function(kernel, unifKernel = NULL, celltypes, communication_type = "D", bundle = TRUE,
619	                                    patient_names = NULL, Dcell = NULL, norm = FALSE, patient_idx = NULL, zero_threshold = 1) {
620	
621	  # Subset patients if requested
622	  if (!is.null(patient_idx)) {
623	    kernel <- kernel[,,patient_idx, drop = FALSE]
624	    if (!is.null(unifKernel)) unifKernel <- unifKernel[,,patient_idx, drop = FALSE]
625	    if (!is.null(patient_names)) patient_names <- patient_names[patient_idx]
626	    if (!is.null(Dcell)) Dcell <- Dcell[patient_idx, , drop = FALSE]
627	  }
628	
629	  .compute_one_type <- function(comm) {
630	    comm <- toupper(comm)
631	
632	    if (comm %in% c("D", "W", "TT") && is.null(Dcell) && is.null(unifKernel)) {
633	      stop("Dcell (cell abundance matrix) is required to compute raw (unnormalized) ", comm, " features.")
634	    }
635	
636	    if (comm == "D") {
637	      calculateDirect(kernel = kernel, unifKernel = unifKernel, cells = celltypes, Dcell = Dcell, bundle = bundle, patient_names = patient_names, zero_threshold = zero_threshold)
638	
639	    } else if (comm == "W") {
640	      calculateWedges(kernel = kernel, unifKernel = unifKernel, cells = celltypes, Dcell = Dcell, bundle = bundle, patient_names = patient_names, zero_threshold = zero_threshold)
641	
642	    } else if (comm == "TT") {
643	      # trust/cycle triangles (directed): use bundle = FALSE in computeTriangles
644	      computeTriangles(kernel = kernel, cell_names = celltypes, Dcell = Dcell,
645	                       patient_names = if (!is.null(patient_names)) patient_names else paste0("Patient_", seq_len(dim(kernel)[3])),
646	                       unifKernel = unifKernel, norm = norm, bundle = FALSE, zero_threshold = zero_threshold)
647	
648	    } else if (comm == "GSCC") {
649	      if (is.null(Dcell)) stop("Dcell (cell abundance matrix) is required for GSCC computation.")
650	      # computeGSCC expects patient_names and Dcell rows == patients
651	      computeGSCC(kernel = kernel, Dcell = Dcell,
652	                 cell_names = celltypes,
653	                 patient_names = if (!is.null(patient_names)) patient_names else paste0("Patient_", seq_len(nrow(Dcell))),
654	                 unifKernel = unifKernel, norm = norm)
655	
656	    } else {
657	      stop("Unsupported communication_type. Use D, W, TT, or GSCC.")
658	    }
659	  }
660	
661	  if (length(communication_type) > 1) {
662	    out <- lapply(communication_type, .compute_one_type)
663	    names(out) <- communication_type
664	    return(out)
665	  }
666	
667	  return(.compute_one_type(communication_type))
668	}

670	#' Run the full kernel-based RaCInG workflow
671	#'
672	#' @param counts Gene-by-sample count matrix. Required when `input_data` is not
673	#'   supplied; ignored otherwise.
674	#' @param output_folder Directory used to write and read intermediate input files.
675	#' @param deconv Optional patient-by-cell-type abundance matrix. If omitted, it
676	#'   is computed via `multideconv::compute.deconvolution()` followed by
677	#'   `multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()` (which identifies and
678	#'   collapses correlated cell-type subgroups) and
679	#'   `multideconv::standardize_celltype_colnames()`. See [prepare_input_files()].
680	#' @param cc_network Optional ligand-receptor prior network. If omitted, it is
681	#'   retrieved via `liana::get_curated_omni()`. See [prepare_input_files()].
682	#' @param fun_LR Function combining a ligand's and receptor's expression
683	#'   values (as a length-2 vector) into one interaction strength. Default
684	#'   `min`: the weaker-expressed partner limits the interaction. Any function
685	#'   collapsing 2 values to 1 works, e.g. `prod` for the product of the two
686	#'   instead.
687	#' @param cell_expr_profile Optional gene-by-cell-type expression profile
688	#'   matrix. If omitted, it is estimated from `counts` and `deconv` via
689	#'   per-gene non-negative least squares. See [prepare_input_files()].
690	#' @param expr_threshold Minimum expression (in linear TPM, not log-scale)
