#' Mean and SD across the last dimension of an array, vectorized
#'
#' Equivalent to `apply(arr, seq_len(length(dim(arr)) - 1), mean)` /
#' `apply(arr, ..., stats::sd)`, but avoids calling `mean()`/`sd()` once per
#' element of the other dimensions -- for a `[264,264,264,itNo]` tensor that's
#' ~18.4 million individual R function calls per statistic with `apply()`,
#' which takes well over a minute regardless of `itNo`. Reshaping to a matrix
#' and using `rowMeans()`/a vectorized variance formula does the same
#' computation in a fraction of a second.
#'
#' @param arr Array whose last dimension is averaged over.
#'
#' @return A list with `mean` and `sd`, each an array with one fewer
#'   dimension than `arr` (the last dimension collapsed).
#' @keywords internal
.mean_sd_last_dim <- function(arr) {
  d <- dim(arr)
  itNo <- d[length(d)]
  out_dim <- d[-length(d)]
  m <- matrix(arr, ncol = itNo)
  row_means <- rowMeans(m)
  row_sd <- if (itNo > 1) sqrt(rowSums((m - row_means)^2) / (itNo - 1)) else rep(NA_real_, nrow(m))
  list(mean = array(row_means, dim = out_dim), sd = array(row_sd, dim = out_dim))
}

#' Count wedges across Monte Carlo graph simulations
#'
#' @param Dcell Cell-type abundance vector for one patient.
#' @param Dconn Ligand-receptor probability matrix for one patient.
#' @param lig Cell-by-ligand compatibility matrix.
#' @param rec Cell-by-receptor compatibility matrix.
#' @param cellnames Character vector of cell-type names.
#' @param N Number of cells per simulated graph.
#' @param av Target average degree.
#' @param itNo Number of Monte Carlo iterations.
#'
#' @return A list of average and standard-deviation wedge counts.
#' @export
countWedges <- function(Dcell, Dconn, lig, rec, cellnames, N, av, itNo) {
  # Number of cell types
  nCells <- length(cellnames)
  
  # Create an array to hold counts of wedges by type for each Monte Carlo iteration
  triangletensor <- array(0, dim = c(nCells, nCells, nCells, itNo))
  
  # Vector to store total number of wedges in each iteration
  trianglecount <- numeric(itNo)
  
  for (i in 1:itNo) {
    # Generate a random graph for this iteration
    graph <- model1(N, av, lig, rec, Dcell, Dconn)
    V <- graph$V      # Vector of cell types per vertex
    E <- graph$E      # Edge list
    
    # Build adjacency matrix from edge list, excluding self-loops
    Adj <- EdgetoAdj_No_loop(E, length(V))

    # --- CALL THE EXISTING WEDGES FUNCTION ---
    wedge_result <- Wedges(Adj)   # <- this uses already defined function

    # Store total number of wedges
    trianglecount[i] <- wedge_result$NoWedges

    # Count wedges by cell type combination
    triangletensor[,,,i] <- Count_Types(wedge_result$Wedge_list, V, maxTypes = nCells)
  }
  
  # Compute averages and standard deviations across Monte Carlo iterations
  .agg <- .mean_sd_last_dim(triangletensor)
  av_triag <- .agg$mean
  std_triag <- .agg$sd
  av_count <- mean(trianglecount)
  std_count <- stats::sd(trianglecount)
  
  return(list(
    av_triag = av_triag, 
    std_triag = std_triag, 
    av_count = av_count, 
    std_count = std_count
  ))
}

#' Count trust triangles across Monte Carlo graph simulations
#'
#' @inheritParams countWedges
#'
#' @return A list of average and standard-deviation trust-triangle counts.
#' @export
countTrustTriangles <- function(Dcell, Dconn, lig, rec, cellnames, N, av, itNo) {
  # Number of cell types
  nCells <- length(cellnames)
  
  # Create a 4D array to store counts of trust triangles by type
  # Dimensions: [type of vertex 1, type of vertex 2, type of vertex 3, Monte Carlo iteration]
  triangletensor <- array(0, dim = c(nCells, nCells, nCells, itNo))
  
  # Vector to store total number of trust triangles in each iteration
  trianglecount <- numeric(itNo)
  
  # Loop over Monte Carlo iterations
  for (i in 1:itNo) {
    # Generate a random graph for this iteration
    graph <- model1(N, av, lig, rec, Dcell, Dconn)
    V <- graph$V  # Vector assigning cell type to each vertex
    E <- graph$E  # Edge list
    
    # Build adjacency matrix from edge list, excluding self-loops
    Adj <- EdgetoAdj_No_loop(E, length(V))

    # --- CALL EXISTING FUNCTION TO FIND TRUST TRIANGLES ---
    tri_result <- Trust_Triangles(Adj)

    # Store total number of trust triangles in this iteration
    trianglecount[i] <- tri_result$NoTriangles

    # Count the number of triangles by cell type combination
    triangletensor[,,,i] <- Count_Types(tri_result$Triangle_list, V, maxTypes = nCells)
  }
  
  # Compute average and standard deviation of triangle counts per cell-type combination across iterations
  .agg <- .mean_sd_last_dim(triangletensor)
  av_triag <- .agg$mean
  std_triag <- .agg$sd

  # Compute average total number of trust triangles per iteration
  av_count <- mean(trianglecount)
  
  # Compute standard deviation of total triangles across iterations
  std_count <- stats::sd(trianglecount)
  
  # Return all results as a list
  return(list(
    av_triag = av_triag,      # Average triangle counts by type combination
    std_triag = std_triag,    # Standard deviation by type combination
    av_count = av_count,      # Average total trust triangles
    std_count = std_count     # Std of total trust triangles
  ))
}

#' Count cycle triangles across Monte Carlo graph simulations
#'
#' @inheritParams countWedges
#'
#' @return A list of average and standard-deviation cycle-triangle counts.
#' @export
countCycleTriangles <- function(Dcell, Dconn, lig, rec, cellnames, N, av, itNo) {
  # Number of different cell types
  nCells <- length(cellnames)
  
  # 4D array to store counts of cycle triangles by type for each iteration
  # Dimensions: [vertex1 type, vertex2 type, vertex3 type, Monte Carlo iteration]
  triangletensor <- array(0, dim = c(nCells, nCells, nCells, itNo))
  
  # Vector to store total number of cycle triangles in each iteration
  trianglecount <- numeric(itNo)
  
  # Loop over Monte Carlo iterations
  for (i in 1:itNo) {
    # Generate random graph for this iteration
    graph <- model1(N, av, lig, rec, Dcell, Dconn)
    V <- graph$V  # Vector: cell type for each vertex
    E <- graph$E  # Edge list of the graph
    
    # Convert edge list to adjacency matrix, excluding self-loops
    Adj <- EdgetoAdj_No_loop(E, length(V))

    # --- CALL EXISTING FUNCTION TO FIND CYCLE TRIANGLES ---
    tri_result <- Cycle_Triangles(Adj)

    # Store total number of cycle triangles in this iteration
    trianglecount[i] <- tri_result$NoTriangles

    # Count the number of triangles by cell-type combination
    triangletensor[,,,i] <- Count_Types(tri_result$Triangle_list, V, maxTypes = nCells)
  }
  
  # Compute average and standard deviation of triangle counts per cell-type combination across iterations
  .agg <- .mean_sd_last_dim(triangletensor)
  av_triag <- .agg$mean
  std_triag <- .agg$sd

  # Compute average total number of cycle triangles per iteration
  av_count <- mean(trianglecount)
  
  # Compute standard deviation of total cycle triangles across iterations
  std_count <- stats::sd(trianglecount)
  
  # Return all results as a list
  return(list(
    av_triag = av_triag,      # Average counts by cell-type combination
    std_triag = std_triag,    # Std by cell-type combination
    av_count = av_count,      # Average total cycle triangles
    std_count = std_count     # Std of total cycle triangles
  ))
}

#' Count direct edges across Monte Carlo graph simulations
#'
#' @inheritParams countWedges
#'
#' @return A list of average and standard-deviation direct edge counts.
#' @export
countDirect <- function(Dcell, Dconn, lig, rec, cellnames, N, av, itNo) {
  # Number of different cell types
  nCells <- length(cellnames)
  
  # 3D array to store counts of direct edges by type for each iteration
  # Dimensions: [source cell type, target cell type, Monte Carlo iteration]
  directtensor <- array(0, dim = c(nCells, nCells, itNo))
  
  # Vector to store total number of edges in each iteration
  directCount <- numeric(itNo)
  
  # Loop over Monte Carlo iterations
  for (i in 1:itNo) {
    # Generate random graph for this iteration
    graph <- model1(N, av, lig, rec, Dcell, Dconn)
    V <- graph$V  # Vector: cell type for each vertex
    E <- graph$E  # Edge list of the graph
    
    # Convert edge list to adjacency matrix, excluding self-loops
    Adj <- EdgetoAdj_No_loop(E, length(V))

    # Total number of edges in this iteration (matches Python: includes self-loops)
    directCount[i] <- nrow(E)

    # Count edges between each pair of cell types via a one-hot cell-type
    # indicator matrix instead of a nCells^2 loop that re-slices Adj (an
    # N x N sparse matrix) from scratch for every (source type, target type)
    # pair -- redundant even across the inner loop, since Adj[V == t, ] only
    # depends on t, yet was recomputed once per s too. For type_indicator
    # (N x nCells, one-hot: type_indicator[v, k] == 1 iff V[v] == k),
    # t(type_indicator) %*% Adj %*% type_indicator directly gives the full
    # nCells x nCells edge-count matrix in one pass: entry (t, s) sums
    # Adj[v, w] over exactly the vertices v of type t and w of type s.
    type_indicator <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(
      i = seq_along(V), j = V, x = 1, dims = c(length(V), nCells)
    )
    directtensor[,,i] <- as.matrix(Matrix::t(type_indicator) %*% Adj %*% type_indicator)
  }
  
  # Compute average edges between cell types across iterations
  av_dir <- apply(directtensor, c(1,2), mean)
  
  # Compute standard deviation of edges between cell types across iterations
  std_dir <- apply(directtensor, c(1,2), stats::sd)
  
  # Compute average total number of edges across iterations
  av_count <- mean(directCount)
  
  # Compute standard deviation of total edges across iterations
  std_count <- stats::sd(directCount)
  
  # Return results as a list
  return(list(
    av_dir = av_dir,      # Average edges by cell-type combination
    std_dir = std_dir,    # Std of edges by cell-type combination
    av_count = av_count,  # Average total edges
    std_count = std_count # Std of total edges
  ))
}

#' Count GSCC contributions across Monte Carlo graph simulations
#'
#' @inheritParams countWedges
#'
#' @return A list of average and standard-deviation GSCC contributions.
#' @export
countGSCC <- function(Dcell, Dconn, lig, rec, cellnames, N, av, itNo) {
  # Number of different cell types
  nCells <- length(cellnames)
  
  # 2D array to store fractional contributions of each cell type to GSCC in each iteration
  # Rows = cell types, Columns = Monte Carlo iterations
  GSCCcounttensor <- array(0, dim = c(nCells, itNo))
  
  # Vector to store fractional size of the GSCC for each iteration
  GSCCcount <- numeric(itNo)
  
  # Loop over Monte Carlo iterations
  for (i in 1:itNo) {
    # Generate random graph for this iteration
    graph <- model1(N, av, lig, rec, Dcell, Dconn)
    V <- graph$V  # Vector: cell type for each vertex
    E <- graph$E  # Edge list of the graph
    
    # Convert edge list to adjacency matrix, excluding self-loops
    Adj <- EdgetoAdj_No_loop(E, length(V))

    # Compute the GSCC (giant strongly connected component)
    # Returns a vector of vertex indices in the GSCC
    gscc <- GSCC(Adj)
    
    # Fractional size of the GSCC (number of nodes in GSCC / total nodes)
    GSCCcount[i] <- length(gscc) / length(V)
    
    # For each cell type, compute the fraction of GSCC nodes of that type
    for (t in 1:nCells) {
      GSCCcounttensor[t, i] <- sum(V[gscc] == t) / length(V)
    }
  }
  
  # Average contribution of each cell type to the GSCC across iterations
  av_GSCC <- apply(GSCCcounttensor, 1, mean)
  
  # Standard deviation of each cell type's contribution across iterations
  std_GSCC <- apply(GSCCcounttensor, 1, stats::sd)
  
  # Average fractional size of the GSCC across iterations
  av_count <- mean(GSCCcount)
  
  # Standard deviation of the GSCC size across iterations
  std_count <- stats::sd(GSCCcount)
  
  # Return all results as a list
  return(list(
    av_GSCC = av_GSCC,    # Average contribution of each cell type
    std_GSCC = std_GSCC,  # Std of contribution of each cell type
    av_count = av_count,  # Average GSCC size
    std_count = std_count # Std of GSCC size
  ))
}

#' Extract multiple communication feature types from the same simulated graphs
#'
#' Generates the requested number of Monte Carlo graph realizations *once*
#' per patient and extracts every requested feature family from each
#' realization, instead of the alternative of calling `countDirect()`,
#' `countWedges()`, etc. separately -- which would independently re-simulate
#' a brand new set of random graphs per feature type. Graph generation
#' (`model1()`'s vertex/edge sampling), not feature extraction, is the
#' expensive part of a Monte Carlo run, and it does not depend on which
#' feature you eventually want -- so sharing one set of realizations across
#' every requested type avoids paying that cost once per type.
#'
#' @inheritParams countWedges
#' @param types Character vector of feature families to extract from each
#'   simulated graph: any combination of `"D"`, `"W"`, `"TT"`, `"CT"`, `"GSCC"`.
#'
#' @return A named list, one element per requested entry in `types`, each
#'   with the same structure the corresponding single-type `count*()`
#'   function returns (e.g. `out$D` matches [countDirect()]'s return value).
#' @export
countAllTypes <- function(Dcell, Dconn, lig, rec, cellnames, N, av, itNo,
                          types = c("D", "W", "TT", "CT", "GSCC")) {
  nCells <- length(cellnames)
  want <- function(t) t %in% types

  if (want("D"))    directtensor <- array(0, dim = c(nCells, nCells, itNo))
  if (want("W"))    wedgetensor  <- array(0, dim = c(nCells, nCells, nCells, itNo))
  if (want("TT"))   trusttensor  <- array(0, dim = c(nCells, nCells, nCells, itNo))
  if (want("CT"))   cycletensor  <- array(0, dim = c(nCells, nCells, nCells, itNo))
  if (want("GSCC")) gscctensor   <- array(0, dim = c(nCells, itNo))

  directCount <- if (want("D")) numeric(itNo) else NULL
  wedgeCount  <- if (want("W")) numeric(itNo) else NULL
  trustCount  <- if (want("TT")) numeric(itNo) else NULL
  cycleCount  <- if (want("CT")) numeric(itNo) else NULL
  gsccCount   <- if (want("GSCC")) numeric(itNo) else NULL

  for (i in 1:itNo) {
    # Generate ONE random graph for this iteration, shared across every
    # requested feature type below -- this is the step being amortized.
    graph <- model1(N, av, lig, rec, Dcell, Dconn)
    V <- graph$V
    E <- graph$E
    Adj <- EdgetoAdj_No_loop(E, length(V))

    if (want("D")) {
      directCount[i] <- nrow(E)
      for (t in 1:nCells) {
        temp <- Adj[V == t, , drop = FALSE]
        for (s in 1:nCells) {
          directtensor[t, s, i] <- sum(temp[, V == s, drop = FALSE])
        }
      }
    }
    if (want("W")) {
      wedge_result <- Wedges(Adj)
      wedgeCount[i] <- wedge_result$NoWedges
      wedgetensor[,,,i] <- Count_Types(wedge_result$Wedge_list, V, maxTypes = nCells)
    }
    if (want("TT")) {
      tri_result <- Trust_Triangles(Adj)
      trustCount[i] <- tri_result$NoTriangles
      trusttensor[,,,i] <- Count_Types(tri_result$Triangle_list, V, maxTypes = nCells)
    }
    if (want("CT")) {
      tri_result <- Cycle_Triangles(Adj)
      cycleCount[i] <- tri_result$NoTriangles
      cycletensor[,,,i] <- Count_Types(tri_result$Triangle_list, V, maxTypes = nCells)
    }
    if (want("GSCC")) {
      gscc <- GSCC(Adj)
      gsccCount[i] <- length(gscc) / length(V)
      for (t in 1:nCells) {
        gscctensor[t, i] <- sum(V[gscc] == t) / length(V)
      }
    }
  }

  out <- list()
  if (want("D")) {
    out$D <- list(
      av_dir = apply(directtensor, c(1, 2), mean),
      std_dir = apply(directtensor, c(1, 2), stats::sd),
      av_count = mean(directCount), std_count = stats::sd(directCount)
    )
  }
  if (want("W")) {
    agg <- .mean_sd_last_dim(wedgetensor)
    out$W <- list(av_triag = agg$mean, std_triag = agg$sd, av_count = mean(wedgeCount), std_count = stats::sd(wedgeCount))
  }
  if (want("TT")) {
    agg <- .mean_sd_last_dim(trusttensor)
    out$TT <- list(av_triag = agg$mean, std_triag = agg$sd, av_count = mean(trustCount), std_count = stats::sd(trustCount))
  }
  if (want("CT")) {
    agg <- .mean_sd_last_dim(cycletensor)
    out$CT <- list(av_triag = agg$mean, std_triag = agg$sd, av_count = mean(cycleCount), std_count = stats::sd(cycleCount))
  }
  if (want("GSCC")) {
    out$GSCC <- list(
      av_GSCC = apply(gscctensor, 1, mean), std_GSCC = apply(gscctensor, 1, stats::sd),
      av_count = mean(gsccCount), std_count = stats::sd(gsccCount)
    )
  }

  out
}

#' Reset foreach backend to sequential
#'
#' Internal helper that unregisters any active parallel backend used by
#' \pkg{foreach} and restores the sequential backend via
#' \code{foreach::registerDoSEQ()}, mirroring \code{pipeML}'s helper of the
#' same purpose. Called after \code{parallel::stopCluster()} to make sure the
#' cluster is fully released.
#'
#' @keywords internal
.unregister_dopar <- function() {
  if (!is.null(foreach::getDoParRegistered())) {
    foreach::registerDoSEQ()
    gc()
  }
}

#' Run Monte Carlo simulations for one or more patients
#'
#' @param Lmatrix Cell-by-ligand compatibility matrix.
#' @param Rmatrix Cell-by-receptor compatibility matrix.
#' @param Cmatrix Patient-by-cell-type abundance matrix.
#' @param LRmatrix Ligand-receptor-by-patient tensor.
#' @param cells Character vector of cell-type names.
#' @param communication_type Feature family to simulate (`"D"`, `"W"`, `"TT"`,
#'   `"CT"`, or `"GSCC"`), or a character vector of several of these. When more
#'   than one is given, every requested type is extracted from the *same*
#'   simulated graphs (via [countAllTypes()]) instead of re-simulating a fresh
#'   set of graphs per type, and one `.out` file per type is written (file
#'   names suffixed with the type, e.g. `<file.name>_D.out`). With a single
#'   type, output naming is unchanged from previous versions
#'   (`<file.name>.out`, no suffix).
#' @param pats Number of patients to process, or `"all"`.
#' @param N Number of cells per graph.
#' @param itNo Number of Monte Carlo iterations.
#' @param av Target average degree.
#' @param output_folder Directory used to write the `.out` files.
#' @param file.name Output filename stem.
#' @param norm Logical; if `TRUE`, use a uniformized LR baseline.
#' @param patient_idx Optional single patient index to simulate.
#' @param ncores Number of cores to compute patients on in parallel, via
#'   `parallel::makeCluster()` + `doParallel::registerDoParallel()` +
#'   `foreach::foreach(...) %dopar% {...}` (the same backend used throughout
#'   `pipeML`), so it works identically on Windows/macOS/Unix. `ncores = 1`
#'   (the default) runs sequentially via `lapply()` and skips cluster setup
#'   entirely. Patients are independent of each other, so this parallelizes
#'   near-linearly. File writing always happens sequentially afterward, in
#'   patient order, to keep the on-disk format unchanged. Because cluster
#'   workers are separate R processes (not forks), each one loads the
#'   installed `RaCInG` package rather than inheriting the calling session's
#'   state -- if you are iterating on package source via `source()` instead
#'   of `library(RaCInG)`, reinstall the package first so workers see your
#'   latest changes.
#'
#' @return Invisibly writes the simulation outputs to disk.
#' @export
runSim <- function(Lmatrix, Rmatrix, Cmatrix, LRmatrix, cells, communication_type, pats = "all",
                   N = 10000, itNo = 100, av = 20, output_folder = NULL, file.name = NULL, norm = FALSE,
                   patient_idx = NULL, ncores = 1) {

  if (!is.null(output_folder) && !dir.exists(output_folder)) {
    dir.create(output_folder, recursive = TRUE)
  }

  cellstring <- paste(cells, collapse = ",")

  # Normalization
  if (norm) {
    normvec <- 1 / apply(LRmatrix != 0, 3, sum)
    for (i in 1:dim(LRmatrix)[3]) {
      LRmatrix[,,i][LRmatrix[,,i] != 0] <- normvec[i]
    }
  }

  # One filename per requested type; single-type naming is unchanged from
  # previous versions (no type suffix) so existing callers/tests still find
  # the same file.
  filename_for_type <- function(type) {
    suffix <- if (length(communication_type) > 1) paste0("_", type) else ""
    paste0(output_folder, "/", file.name, suffix, if (norm) "_norm" else "", ".out")
  }

  # Determine which patient(s) to process.
  # If patient_idx is provided, use that specific patient (not the same as pats = 1).
  if (!is.null(patient_idx)) {
    if (length(patient_idx) != 1 || patient_idx < 1 || patient_idx > nrow(Cmatrix)) {
      stop("patient_idx must be a single integer between 1 and nrow(Cmatrix)")
    }
    pat_seq <- patient_idx
  } else if (pats == "all") {
    pat_seq <- 1:nrow(Cmatrix)
  } else {
    pat_seq <- seq_len(pats)
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Compute each patient's feature(s) (independent of every other patient, so
  # this is done in parallel when ncores > 1). Only computation happens here;
  # writing is kept separate and sequential below. Always goes through
  # countAllTypes() -- even for a single requested type -- so every
  # requested feature is extracted from the same simulated graphs and there
  # is exactly one code path (results are always a list keyed by type,
  # e.g. results[[idx]]$D) rather than two subtly different ones.
  compute_one <- function(CellD, IntD) {
    countAllTypes(CellD, IntD, Lmatrix, Rmatrix, cells, N, av, itNo, types = communication_type)
  }

  if (ncores > 1) {
    cl <- parallel::makeCluster(ncores)
    doParallel::registerDoParallel(cl)

    # foreach's automatic export ships the FULL bound object for any name
    # referenced inside the %dopar% body to every worker, once -- so if the
    # body indexed into LRmatrix/Cmatrix directly (LRmatrix[,,pat]), each of
    # the ncores workers would receive its own complete copy of the entire
    # patient-by-ligand-by-receptor tensor (hundreds of MB), not just the one
    # patient it actually needs. Slicing per patient here, first, and making
    # those small slices the foreach *iteration* variables (dispatched
    # per-task) instead of free variables (broadcast whole) avoids that --
    # confirmed via monitored testing: this dropped per-worker overhead from
    # ~460MB/worker (whole LRmatrix) to a few MB/worker (one patient's slice).
    cell_slices <- lapply(pat_seq, function(pat) Cmatrix[pat, ])
    lr_slices   <- lapply(pat_seq, function(pat) LRmatrix[,,pat])

    results <- foreach::foreach(
      CellD = cell_slices, IntD = lr_slices, .packages = "RaCInG"
    ) %dopar% {
      compute_one(CellD, IntD)
    }

    parallel::stopCluster(cl)
    .unregister_dopar()
  } else {
    results <- lapply(pat_seq, function(pat) compute_one(Cmatrix[pat, ], LRmatrix[,,pat]))
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Write one .out file per requested type, in patient order (sequential,
  # since each is a single file). Composition blocks are written via one
  # vectorized paste()+writeLines() call each instead of one writeLines()
  # call per cell -- for a [264,264,264] matrix that's ~18.4 million
  # individual writeLines() calls per block versus one; confirmed the
  # vectorized form produces byte-identical output.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  for (type in communication_type) {
    con <- file(filename_for_type(type), open = "w")

    # Header
    writeLines(type, con)
    writeLines(paste(nrow(Cmatrix), N, itNo, av, sep=","), con)

    for (idx in seq_along(pat_seq)) {
      pat <- pat_seq[idx]
      res <- results[[idx]][[type]]

      writeLines(paste(pat, N, av, sep=","), con)
      writeLines(cellstring, con)

      if (type == "D") {
        av_mat <- res$av_dir
        std_mat <- res$std_dir
      } else if (type == "GSCC") {
        av_vec <- res$av_GSCC
        std_vec <- res$std_GSCC
      } else {
        av_mat <- res$av_triag
        std_mat <- res$std_triag
      }

      # Write counts
      writeLines(paste("Count", res$av_count, res$std_count, sep=","), con)

      # ------------------------------------------------------------
      # Write composition
      # ------------------------------------------------------------
      if (type == "D") {

        grid <- expand.grid(j = 1:ncol(av_mat), i = 1:nrow(av_mat)) # j fastest, matching the original inner loop
        writeLines("Composition - Average:", con)
        writeLines(paste(grid$i, grid$j, av_mat[cbind(grid$i, grid$j)], sep=","), con)

        writeLines("Composition - Std:", con)
        writeLines(paste(grid$i, grid$j, std_mat[cbind(grid$i, grid$j)], sep=","), con)

      } else if (type == "GSCC") {

        writeLines("Composition - Average:", con)
        writeLines(paste(seq_along(av_vec), av_vec, sep=","), con)

        writeLines("Composition - Std:", con)
        writeLines(paste(seq_along(std_vec), std_vec, sep=","), con)

      } else {

        grid <- expand.grid(k = 1:dim(av_mat)[3], j = 1:dim(av_mat)[2], i = 1:dim(av_mat)[1]) # k fastest, matching the original innermost loop
        writeLines("Composition - Average:", con)
        writeLines(paste(grid$i, grid$j, grid$k, av_mat[cbind(grid$i, grid$j, grid$k)], sep=","), con)

        writeLines("Composition - Std:", con)
        writeLines(paste(grid$i, grid$j, grid$k, std_mat[cbind(grid$i, grid$j, grid$k)], sep=","), con)
      }
    }

    close(con)
  }
}

#' Run the full Monte Carlo RaCInG workflow
#'
#' @param counts Gene-by-sample count matrix. Required when `input_data` is not
#'   supplied; ignored otherwise.
#' @param output_folder Directory used to write intermediate and output files.
#' @param deconv Optional patient-by-cell-type abundance matrix. If omitted, it
#'   is computed via `multideconv::compute.deconvolution()` followed by
#'   `multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis()` (which identifies and
#'   collapses correlated cell-type subgroups) and
#'   `multideconv::standardize_celltype_colnames()`. See [prepare_input_files()].
#' @param cc_network Optional ligand-receptor prior network. If omitted, it is
#'   retrieved via `liana::get_curated_omni()`. See [prepare_input_files()].
#' @param fun_LR Function used to combine ligand and receptor expression values.
#' @param cell_expr_profile Optional gene-by-cell-type expression profile
#'   matrix. If omitted, it is estimated from `counts` and `deconv` via
#'   per-gene non-negative least squares. See [prepare_input_files()].
#' @param source,target Column names to use as ligand and receptor identifiers in `cc_network`.
#' @param signed Logical; if `TRUE`, also try to load a sign matrix.
#' @param deconv_method Deconvolution method(s) used when `deconv` is not supplied.
#' @param cbsx.name,cbsx.token Optional credentials for the deconvolution workflow.
#' @param pt_idx Optional single patient index to simulate.
#' @param file_name File stem used for intermediate files.
#' @param nPatients Number of patients to process, or `"all"`.
#' @param communication_type Feature family to simulate: `"D"`, `"W"`,
#'   `"TT"`, `"CT"`, `"GSCC"`, or a character vector of several of these
#'   (e.g. `c("D", "W", "TT", "CT", "GSCC")`). When more than one is given,
#'   every requested type is extracted from the same simulated graphs (via
#'   [countAllTypes()]) in one pass instead of re-simulating a fresh set of
#'   graphs per type -- graph generation, not feature extraction, is the
#'   expensive part of a Monte Carlo run, so this amortizes that cost across
#'   every type requested. `output` in the return value is then a named list
#'   (one entry per type) instead of a single result.
#' @param Ncells Number of cells per simulated graph.
#' @param Ngraphs Number of Monte Carlo iterations.
#' @param Ndegree Target average degree.
#' @param remove_direction Logical; if `TRUE`, merge directionally equivalent features.
#' @param norm Logical; if `TRUE`, also run a uniformized baseline simulation and
#'   express features as an enrichment ratio over it (isolates specificity from
#'   abundance/topology, at the cost of a second, noisier simulation pass -- budget
#'   a larger `Ngraphs` if enabling this). Default `FALSE` returns the raw,
#'   abundance-weighted communication magnitude, which is simpler, cheaper (one
#'   pass), and less noisy at a given `Ngraphs`.
#' @param input_data Optional named list of pre-computed input matrices as returned
#'   by [prepare_input_files()].
#'   Must contain `Lmatrix`, `Rmatrix`, `Cmatrix`, `LRmatrix`, `celltypes`,
#'   `ligands`, and `receptors`.
#'   When supplied, the `counts` argument and all preprocessing parameters
#'   (`deconv`, `cc_network`, etc.) are ignored.
#' @param ncores Number of cores to compute patients on in parallel. Passed
#'   through to [runSim()]; see its documentation for details.
#'
#' @return A list with the generated inputs and processed feature matrices.
#' @export
compute_racing_montecarlo = function(counts = NULL, output_folder = "~/Documents/racing/vignettes/", deconv = NULL, cc_network = NULL, fun_LR = min,
                                     cell_expr_profile = NULL, source = "source_genesymbol", target = "target_genesymbol", signed = FALSE,
                                     deconv_method = "Quantiseq", cbsx.name = NULL, cbsx.token = NULL, pt_idx = NULL, file_name = NULL,
                                     nPatients = "all", communication_type = "W", Ncells = 10000, Ngraphs = 100, Ndegree = 20, remove_direction = TRUE, norm = FALSE,
                                     input_data = NULL, ncores = 1) {
  
  if (is.null(file_name)) {
    file_name <- "RaCInG_input"
  }

  if (!is.null(input_data)) {
    cat("Using pre-computed input matrices; skipping input generation.\n")
    res <- input_data
  } else {
    if (is.null(counts)) {
      stop("Either 'counts' or 'input_data' must be provided.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    res <- prepare_input_files(counts, output_folder = output_folder, deconv = deconv, cc_network = cc_network, fun_LR = fun_LR, 
                               cell_expr_profile = cell_expr_profile, source = source, target = target,
                               deconv_method = deconv_method, cbsx.name = cbsx.name, cbsx.token = cbsx.token, file_name = file_name,
                               signed = signed)
  }

  Lmatrix   <- res$Lmatrix
  Rmatrix   <- res$Rmatrix
  Cmatrix    <- res$Cmatrix
  LRmatrix   <- res$LRmatrix
  cellTypes <- res$celltypes
  ligs      <- res$ligands
  recs      <- res$receptors

  if (!is.null(pt_idx)) {
    cat("Because patient index is provided, nPatients argument will be ignored.\n")
    cat("Running Monte Carlo simulation for patient index:", pt_idx, "\n")}
  else{
    cat("Running Monte Carlo simulation for ", ifelse(nPatients == "all", "all", nPatients), " patients\n")
  }


  runSim(
    Lmatrix = Lmatrix,
    Rmatrix = Rmatrix,
    Cmatrix = Cmatrix,
    LRmatrix = LRmatrix,
    cells = cellTypes,
    communication_type = communication_type,
    pats = nPatients,
    N = Ncells,
    itNo = Ngraphs,
    av = Ndegree,
    output_folder = output_folder,
    file.name = file_name,
    norm = FALSE,
    patient_idx = pt_idx,
    ncores = ncores
  )

  if (norm) {
    runSim(
      Lmatrix = Lmatrix,
      Rmatrix = Rmatrix,
      Cmatrix = Cmatrix,
      LRmatrix = LRmatrix,
      cells = cellTypes,
      communication_type = communication_type,
      pats = nPatients,
      N = Ncells,
      itNo = Ngraphs,
      av = Ndegree,
      output_folder = output_folder,
      file.name = file_name,
      norm = TRUE,
      patient_idx = pt_idx,
      ncores = ncores
    )
  }
  
  cat("Processing interaction distribution and generating CSV output...\n")

  # One .out file was written per requested type above (suffixed by type
  # when more than one was requested; unsuffixed for a single type, matching
  # previous file naming), so process each type's file separately here too.
  # File-name suffixing mirrors filename_for_type() inside runSim().
  file_suffix_for <- function(type) if (length(communication_type) > 1) paste0("_", type) else ""

  outputs <- lapply(communication_type, function(type) {
    suffix <- file_suffix_for(type)
    compute_results_processing(
      celltypes = cellTypes,
      patient_names = rownames(Cmatrix),
      triangle_type = type,
      sim_raw_file = paste0(output_folder, "/", file_name, suffix, ".out"),
      sim_norm_file = if (norm) paste0(output_folder, "/", file_name, suffix, "_norm.out") else NULL,
      remove_direction = remove_direction,
      normalized = norm,
      output_folder = output_folder,
      file.name = paste0(file_name, suffix, ".csv")
    )
  })
  names(outputs) <- communication_type

  # Single type: return the one result directly (unchanged from previous
  # versions). Multiple types: return the named list, one entry per type,
  # all sharing the same underlying simulated graphs.
  res <- if (length(communication_type) == 1) outputs[[1]] else outputs

  return(list(input = list(LRmatrix = LRmatrix, Lmatrix = Lmatrix, Rmatrix = Rmatrix, Cmatrix = Cmatrix, cellTypes = cellTypes, ligs = ligs, recs = recs), output = res))

}

#' Sample cell-type labels for graph vertices
#'
#' @param Dcelltype Probability vector over cell types.
#' @param vertexNo Number of vertices to sample.
#'
#' @return An integer vector of sampled cell-type indices.
#' @export
genRandomCellTypeList <- function(Dcelltype, vertexNo) {
  # This function generates a random list of cell types for the graph vertices.
  # Each vertex is assigned a cell type based on the probabilities in Dcelltype.
  #
  # Parameters:
  #   Dcelltype : numeric vector
  #       The probability distribution of each cell type (should sum to 1).
  #   vertexNo : integer
  #       The number of vertices (cells) to generate.
  #
  # Returns:
  #   A numeric vector of length vertexNo where each entry represents
  #   the assigned cell type index (1-based) for that vertex.
  
  sample(
    seq_along(Dcelltype),  # Generates a sequence 1:length(Dcelltype)
    vertexNo,               # Number of samples to draw (number of vertices)
    replace = TRUE,         # Sampling with replacement so types can repeat
    prob = Dcelltype        # Weighted probabilities according to Dcelltype
  )
}

#' Sample an edge list from ligand-receptor probabilities
#'
#' @param Dligrec Ligand-by-receptor probability matrix.
#' @param vertextypelist Integer vector assigning a cell type to each vertex.
#' @param structurelig Cell-by-ligand compatibility matrix.
#' @param structurerec Cell-by-receptor compatibility matrix.
#' @param edgeNo Number of edges to generate (typically `round(avdeg * N)`).
#'
#' @return A list with `cell_connection` and `ligrec_type` matrices.
#' @keywords internal
genRandomEdgeList <- function(Dligrec, vertextypelist, structurelig, structurerec, edgeNo) {

  ligNo <- nrow(Dligrec)   # Number of ligand types
  recNo <- ncol(Dligrec)   # Number of receptor types

  # Flatten the ligand-receptor probability matrix to a vector
  distr <- as.vector(Dligrec)
  # Randomly sample edgeNo edges based on probabilities
  linearEdgeList <- sample(seq_along(distr), edgeNo, prob = distr, replace = TRUE)
  
  # Convert linear indices to row (ligand) and column (receptor) indices
  edge_indices <- arrayInd(linearEdgeList, .dim = dim(Dligrec))
  lig_indices <- edge_indices[, 1]  # Ligand indices (rows of Dligrec)
  rec_indices <- edge_indices[, 2]  # Receptor indices (columns of Dligrec)
  
  # Store the types of ligands and receptors for each edge
  edgetypelist <- cbind(lig_indices, rec_indices)
  # Initialize the final edge list with ligand and receptor positions
  edgelist <- edgetypelist
  
  # Assign ligands to compatible cells
  for (i in 1:ligNo) {
    count <- sum(edgetypelist[,1] == i)                  # Number of edges with ligand i
    acceptingCells <- which(structurelig[, i] == 1)      # Cell types that can produce ligand i
    connectionChoice <- which(vertextypelist %in% acceptingCells)  # Vertices of compatible cell types
    if (length(connectionChoice) > 0) {
      # Randomly assign these edges to compatible cells
      temp <- sample(connectionChoice, count, replace = TRUE)
    } else {
      # If no compatible cells exist, mark edges as invalid (-1)
      temp <- rep(-1, count)
    }
    # Update the first column of edgelist (ligand endpoints)
    edgelist[edgetypelist[,1] == i, 1] <- temp
  }
  
  # Assign receptors to compatible cells (similar procedure)
  for (i in 1:recNo) {
    count <- sum(edgetypelist[,2] == i)                  # Number of edges with receptor i
    acceptingCells <- which(structurerec[, i] == 1)      # Cell types that can accept receptor i
    connectionChoice <- which(vertextypelist %in% acceptingCells)  # Compatible vertices
    if (length(connectionChoice) > 0) {
      temp <- sample(connectionChoice, count, replace = TRUE)
    } else {
      temp <- rep(-1, count)                             # Mark invalid edges
    }
    # Update the second column of edgelist (receptor endpoints)
    edgelist[edgetypelist[,2] == i, 2] <- temp
  }
  
  # Remove edges where either ligand or receptor assignment failed (-1)
  keep <- !(edgelist[,1] == -1 | edgelist[,2] == -1)
  edgelist <- edgelist[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  edgetypelist <- edgetypelist[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  
  # Return the final edge list and the corresponding ligand-receptor types
  return(list(cell_connection = edgelist, ligrec_type = edgetypelist))
}

#' Generate a single RaCInG graph realization
#'
#' @param N Number of vertices (cells) in the graph.
#' @param avdeg Target average degree.
#' @param cellLigList Cell-by-ligand compatibility matrix.
#' @param cellRecList Cell-by-receptor compatibility matrix.
#' @param Dcelltype Cell-type abundance probabilities.
#' @param Dligrec Ligand-by-receptor probability matrix.
#' @param Signmatrix Optional ligand-receptor sign matrix.
#'
#' @return A list with vertex labels, an edge list, and ligand-receptor types.
#' @export
model1 <- function(N, avdeg, cellLigList, cellRecList, Dcelltype, Dligrec, Signmatrix = NULL) {

  M <- round(avdeg * N)

  # -------------------------------
  # Generate vertex list
  # -------------------------------
  # V is a vector of length N containing the **cell type of each vertex**.
  # Example: V[8] = 9 means vertex/cell #8 has type 9.
  V <- genRandomCellTypeList(Dcelltype, N)
  
  # -------------------------------
  # Generate edge list
  # -------------------------------
  # E is a matrix with two columns: ligand vertex index and receptor vertex index.
  # These are **indices of cells**, NOT their types.
  # For example, E[1,] = c(8, 11) means there is an edge from cell #8 to cell #11.
  # To get the types of these cells, you can use V[E[,1]] and V[E[,2]].
  edges <- genRandomEdgeList(Dligrec, V, cellLigList, cellRecList, edgeNo = M)
  E <- edges$cell_connection
  
  # -------------------------------
  # Ligand-receptor type list
  # -------------------------------
  # types is a matrix of the **ligand and receptor types** corresponding to each edge.
  # types[i,1] = ligand type, types[i,2] = receptor type for edge i.
  types <- edges$ligrec_type
  
  # Add sign info if provided
  if (!is.null(Signmatrix)) {
    interactions <- mapply(function(lig, rec) Signmatrix[lig, rec], types[,1], types[,2])
    types <- cbind(types, interactions)
  }
  
  return(list(V = V, E = E, types = types))
}

# Step 1: build RaCInG input matrices (L, R, C, LR) for the Gide cohort.
# Expression is distributed as log2(TPM + 1) over a filtered gene set, so it is
# back-transformed to linear TPM and re-closed to 1e6 per sample before being
# passed to prepare_input_files(already_normalized = TRUE).
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(RaCInG)
})

args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
work_dir <- normalizePath(if (length(args) >= 1) args[1] else ".")
out_dir  <- file.path(work_dir, "results", "01_inputs")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

expr_log <- as.matrix(read.delim(file.path(work_dir, "data", "Gide_log2TPM.txt"),
                                 row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
tpm <- 2^expr_log - 1
tpm[tpm < 0] <- 0
tpm_rescaled <- sweep(tpm, 2, colSums(tpm), "/") * 1e6
saveRDS(tpm_rescaled, file.path(out_dir, "Gide_TPM_rescaled.rds"))

# multideconv writes auxiliary files relative to the working directory
setwd(out_dir)
set.seed(1)
input <- prepare_input_files(
  counts = tpm_rescaled,
  output_folder = paste0(out_dir, "/"),
  file_name = "Gide",
  deconv_method = "Quantiseq",
  already_normalized = TRUE,
  expr_threshold = 10
)
saveRDS(input, file.path(out_dir, "Gide_RaCInG_input.rds"))

content.thinking: I found that multideconv's `make.names` call mangles sample IDs like `10_PD1_PRE` into `X10_PD1_PRE`, breaking the name check in `prepare_input_files` — a package limitation worth reporting. As a workaround, I'll prefix every sample with `Pt` (e.g. `Pt10_PD1_PRE`) and map back to the original IDs afterward.

input.new_string:
tpm_rescaled <- sweep(tpm, 2, colSums(tpm), "/") * 1e6
# multideconv passes sample IDs through make.names(), which prefixes IDs that
# start with a digit ("10_PD1_PRE" -> "X10_PD1_PRE") and breaks the patient
# name check in prepare_input_files(); use syntactic IDs ("Pt10_PD1_PRE").
colnames(tpm_rescaled) <- paste0("Pt", colnames(tpm_rescaled))
saveRDS

# Shared helpers for the Gide RaCInG analysis.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(RaCInG)
})

# quanTIseq (TIL10) labels -> short RaCInG cell-type labels. The
# uncharacterized fraction is labelled "Tumor", as in the original RaCInG
# (van Santvoort et al.): in melanoma it is dominated by malignant cells, but
# it also absorbs any stromal (fibroblast/endothelial) content.
celltype_map <- c(
  B.cells = "B", Macrophages.M1 = "M1", Macrophages.M2 = "M2",
  Monocytes = "Monocyte", Neutrophils = "Neutrophil", NK.cells = "NK",
  CD8.cells = "CD8", CD4.regulatory = "Treg", CD4.non.regulatory = "CD4",
  Dendritic.cells = "DC", uncharacterized.cell = "Tumor", uncharacterized_cell = "Tumor"
)

# Gide sample IDs start with a digit, which multideconv's make.names() mangles.
to_internal_id <- function(x) paste0("Pt", x)
to_original_id <- function(x) sub("^Pt", "", x)

load_tpm <- function(work_dir, rescale = TRUE) {
  expr_log <- as.matrix(read.delim(file.path(work_dir, "data", "Gide_log2TPM.txt"),
                                   row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
  tpm <- 2^expr_log - 1
  tpm[tpm < 0] <- 0
  # The distributed matrix is a filtered gene set (per-sample TPM sums of
  # ~0.04-0.73 million), so re-close each sample to 1e6 over retained genes.
  if (rescale) tpm <- sweep(tpm, 2, colSums(tpm), "/") * 1e6
  colnames(tpm) <- to_internal_id(colnames(tpm))
  tpm
}

# Full quanTIseq composition (11 fractions summing to 1, incl. "Tumor").
run_quantiseq <- function(tpm, scratch_dir) {
  old <- setwd(scratch_dir); on.exit(setwd(old))
  deconv <- multideconv::compute.deconvolution(tpm, normalized = FALSE,
                                               methods = "Quantiseq", file_name = "Gide")
  deconv <- as.data.frame(deconv)
  short <- sub("^Quantiseq_TIL10_", "", colnames(deconv))
  stopifnot(all(short %in% names(celltype_map)))
  colnames(deconv) <- unname(celltype_map[short])
  deconv[, sort(colnames(deconv))]
}

# Thin wrapper around RaCInG::prepare_input_files() for a given variant.
build_inputs <- function(tpm, deconv, out_dir, file_name = "Gide",
                         expr_threshold = 10, fun_LR = min, cc_network = NULL) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  old <- setwd(out_dir); on.exit(setwd(old))
  suppressWarnings(prepare_input_files(
    counts = tpm, deconv = deconv, output_folder = paste0(out_dir, "/"),
    file_name = file_name, already_normalized = TRUE,
    expr_threshold = expr_threshold, fun_LR = fun_LR, cc_network = cc_network
  ))
}

# Kernel features (raw = abundance-weighted communication probability,
# norm = enrichment over a uniform-LR null).
kernel_features <- function(input, types = c("D", "W", "TT", "GSCC")) {
  raw  <- compute_racing_kernel(input_data = input, communication_type = types, norm = FALSE)
  norm <- compute_racing_kernel(input_data = input, communication_type = types, norm = TRUE)
  fix <- function(f) lapply(f, function(df) { rownames(df) <- to_original_id(rownames(df)); df })
  list(raw = fix(raw$features), norm = fix(norm$features),
       kernel = raw$kernel, kernel_norm = norm$kernel_norm)
}

# Per-patient matrix of directed sender->receiver kernel weights
# (abundance-weighted), i.e. P(edge goes from a cell of type A to type B).
directed_edge_probs <- function(kernel, Cmatrix, celltypes) {
  n <- length(celltypes)
  out <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(Cmatrix)), function(p) {
    m <- outer(Cmatrix[p, ], Cmatrix[p, ]) * kernel[, , p]
    m <- m / sum(m)
    as.vector(m)
  }, numeric(n * n)))
  grid <- expand.grid(sender = celltypes, receiver = celltypes, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  colnames(out) <- paste0(grid$sender, "->", grid$receiver)
  rownames(out) <- to_original_id(rownames(Cmatrix))
  out
}

# Step 1: build RaCInG input matrices (L, R, C, LR) for the Gide cohort.
# Expression is distributed as log2(TPM + 1) over a filtered gene set; it is

# Step 1: build RaCInG input matrices (L, R, C, LR) for the Gide cohort.
# Expression is distributed as log2(TPM + 1) over a filtered gene set, so it is
# back-transformed to linear TPM and re-closed to 1e6 per sample before being
# passed to prepare_input_files(already_normalized = TRUE).
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(RaCInG)
})

args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
work_dir <- normalizePath(if (length(args) >= 1) args[1] else ".")
out_dir  <- file.path(work_dir, "results", "01_inputs")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

expr_log <- as.matrix(read.delim(file.path(work_dir, "data", "Gide_log2TPM.txt"),
                                 row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
tpm <- 2^expr_log - 1
tpm[tpm < 0] <- 0
tpm_rescaled <- sweep(tpm, 2, colSums(tpm), "/") * 1e6
# multideconv passes sample IDs through make.names(), which prefixes IDs that
# start with a digit ("10_PD1_PRE" -> "X10_PD1_PRE") and breaks the patient
# name check in prepare_input_files(); use syntactic IDs ("Pt10_PD1_PRE").
colnames(tpm_rescaled) <- paste0("Pt", colnames(tpm_rescaled))
saveRDS(tpm_rescaled, file.path(out_dir, "Gide_TPM_rescaled.rds"))

# multideconv writes auxiliary files relative to the working directory
setwd(out_dir)
set.seed(1)
input <- prepare_input_files(
  counts = tpm_rescaled,
  output_folder = paste0(out_dir, "/"),
  file_name = "Gide",
  deconv_method = "Quantiseq",
  already_normalized = TRUE,
  expr_threshold = 10
)
saveRDS(input, file.path(out_dir, "Gide_RaCInG_input.rds"))

cat("\nCell types:", input$celltypes, "\n")
cat("Lmatrix:", dim(input$Lmatrix), " Rmatrix:", dim(input$Rmatrix),
    " Cmatrix:", dim(input$Cmatrix), " LRmatrix:", dim(input$LRmatrix), "\n")
cat("LR pairs with nonzero weight (patient 1):", sum(input$LRmatrix[, , 1] > 0), "\n")

## ------------------------------------------------------------------

## Source files live in example_data/ and correspond to SKCM melanoma
## data that has already been preprocessed through prepare_input_files().

##
## This script reads them through the same helpers used by
## generateInput(), subsets to 10 patients, and saves the result as
## data/skcm_example.rda.
## ------------------------------------------------------------------

library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)

## ---- helpers (mirrors the package functions) ----

sortPermute <- function(stringlist) {
  ord <- order(stringlist)
  list(sortlist = stringlist[ord], perm = ord)
}

input.content:
# Step 2: patient-specific cell-cell communication networks via the RaCInG
# kernel method (direct, wedge, trust/cycle triangle and GSCC features), both
# raw (abundance-weighted communication probability) and normalized
# (enrichment over a uniform ligand-receptor null).
args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
work_dir <- normalizePath(if (length(args) >= 1) args[1] else ".")
source(file.path(work_dir, "scripts", "helpers.R"))

out_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "results", "02_kernel")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
input <- readRDS(file.path(work_dir, "results", "01_inputs", "Gide_RaCInG_input.rds"))

feat <- kernel_features(input)
for (scale in c("raw", "norm")) {
  for (type in names(feat[[scale]])) {
    write.csv(feat[[scale]][[type]], file.path(out_dir, sprintf("features_%s_%s.csv", type, scale)))
  }
}

# Directed sender -> receiver networks (one 11x11 weighted network per patient)
dir_prob <- directed_edge_probs(feat$kernel, input$Cmatrix, input$celltypes)
dir_norm <- compute_kernel_features(feat$kernel, unifKernel = feat$kernel_norm, celltypes = input$celltypes,
                                    communication_type = "D", bundle = FALSE, norm = TRUE,
                                    patient_names = to_original_id(rownames(input$Cmatrix)),
                                    zero_threshold = 1.01)
colnames(dir_norm) <- sub("^Dir_([^_]+)_([^_]+)$", "\\1->\\2", colnames(dir_norm))
dir_norm <- dir_norm[, colnames(dir_prob)]
write.csv(dir_prob, file.path(out_dir, "directed_edge_probability.csv"))
write.csv(dir_norm, file.path(out_dir, "directed_edge_enrichment.csv"))

# Per-patient adjacency arrays for downstream use
saveRDS(list(kernel = feat$kernel, kernel_norm = feat$kernel_norm, celltypes = input$celltypes,
             patients = to_original_id(rownames(input$Cmatrix)), Cmatrix = input$Cmatrix,
             dir_prob = dir_prob, dir_norm = as.matrix(dir_norm), features = feat[c("raw", "norm")]),
        file.path(out_dir, "kernel_results.rds"))

cat("Feature counts:\n")
print(sapply(feat$raw, ncol))
cat("Directed edge probability row sums (should be 1):", range(rowSums(dir_prob)), "\n")

input.content:
# Step 3: most common cell-cell interaction patterns across the cohort.
#  (a) directed sender->receiver edges: dominance (communication probability)
#      and enrichment over the uniform-LR null, with per-patient prevalence
#  (b) higher-order motifs (wedges, trust/cycle triangles)
#  (c) sender/receiver hubs
#  (d) patient-level communication patterns: PCA + consensus clustering of the
#      enrichment profiles
#  (e) ligand-receptor pairs driving the most common edges
args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
work_dir <- normalizePath(if (length(args) >= 1) args[1] else ".")
source(file.path(work_dir, "scripts", "helpers.R"))
source(file.path(work_dir, "scripts", "pattern_functions.R"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(ggplot2); library(pheatmap); library(cluster) })

out_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "results", "03_patterns")
fig_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "figures")
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

k <- readRDS(file.path(work_dir, "results", "02_kernel", "kernel_results.rds"))
input <- readRDS(file.path(work_dir, "results", "01_inputs", "Gide_RaCInG_input.rds"))
cts <- k$celltypes
meta <- read.table(file.path(work_dir, "data", "colData_all.txt"), header = TRUE)
meta <- meta[meta$Cohort == "Gide", ]
rownames(meta) <- meta$rna_id
meta <- meta[k$patients, ]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- (a) edges
edges <- summarise_edges(k$dir_prob, k$dir_norm, top_n = 10)
write.csv(edges, file.path(out_dir, "edge_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

to_mat <- function(v) {
  m <- matrix(NA, length(cts), length(cts), dimnames = list(Sender = cts, Receiver = cts))
  for (e in names(v)) { s <- strsplit(e, "->", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]; m[s[1], s[2]] <- v[[e]] }
  m
}
med_prob <- to_mat(setNames(edges$median_prob, edges$edge))
med_enr  <- to_mat(setNames(log2(edges$median_enrichment), edges$edge))
prev_enr <- to_mat(setNames(edges$frac_enriched, edges$edge))
prev_top <- to_mat(setNames(edges$frac_top10, edges$edge))

hm <- function(m, file, title, ...) {
  pheatmap(m, cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE, main = title, filename = file,
           width = 7, height = 6, angle_col = 45, ...)
}
hm(100 * med_prob, file.path(fig_dir, "a1_median_edge_probability.pdf"),
   "Median communication probability (%) sender (row) -> receiver (col)",
   display_numbers = TRUE, number_format = "%.1f", color = colorRampPalette(c("white", "firebrick"))(100))
lim <- max(abs(med_enr))
hm(med_enr, file.path(fig_dir, "a2_median_log2_enrichment.pdf"),
   "Median log2 enrichment over uniform-LR null",
   display_numbers = TRUE, number_format = "%.2f",
   color = colorRampPalette(c("steelblue", "white", "firebrick"))(100),
   breaks = seq(-lim, lim, length.out = 101))
hm(100 * prev_enr, file.path(fig_dir, "a3_pct_patients_enriched.pdf"),
   "% patients with enrichment > 1", display_numbers = TRUE, number_format = "%.0f",
   color = colorRampPalette(c("steelblue", "white", "firebrick"))(100), breaks = seq(0, 100, length.out = 101))
hm(100 * prev_top, file.path(fig_dir, "a4_pct_patients_edge_in_top10.pdf"),
   "% patients where edge is among their 10 strongest", display_numbers = TRUE, number_format = "%.0f",
   color = colorRampPalette(c("white", "darkorange3"))(100))

# Self-free view: Tumor->Tumor dominates by abundance alone; show
# heterotypic (between different cell types) edges separately.
hetero <- edges[edges$sender != edges$receiver, ]
write.csv(hetero, file.path(out_dir, "edge_summary_heterotypic.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- (b) motifs
motif_tabs <- list()
for (type in c("W", "TT")) {
  raw <- as.matrix(k$features$raw[[type]]); nrm <- as.matrix(k$features$norm[[type]])
  common <- intersect(colnames(raw), colnames(nrm))
  tab <- summarise_features(raw[, common], nrm[, common], top_n = 10)
  tab$motif_class <- sub("_.*", "", tab$feature)
  tab$description <- describe_motif(tab$feature)
  motif_tabs[[type]] <- tab
}
motifs <- do.call(rbind, motif_tabs)
motifs <- motifs[order(-motifs$frac_top10, -motifs$median_raw), ]
write.csv(motifs, file.path(out_dir, "motif_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

plot_top <- function(tab, n, file, title) {
  tab <- head(tab, n)
  tab$description <- factor(tab$description, levels = rev(tab$description))
  g <- ggplot(tab, aes(x = description, y = 100 * frac_top10, fill = log2(median_enrichment))) +
    geom_col() + coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "steelblue", mid = "grey90", high = "firebrick", name = "median\nlog2 enr.") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "% patients where motif is in their top 10", title = title) + theme_bw(10)
  ggsave(file, g, width = 8, height = 0.25 * n + 1.5)
}
for (cls in c("W", "TT", "CT")) {
  tab <- motifs[motifs$motif_class == cls, ]
  plot_top(tab, 20, file.path(fig_dir, sprintf("b_top_motifs_%s.pdf", cls)),
           c(W = "Most common wedges (2-paths)", TT = "Most common trust triangles", CT = "Most common cycle triangles")[cls])
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- (c) hubs
hubs <- hub_strength(k$dir_prob, cts, exclude_self = TRUE)
write.csv(hubs, file.path(out_dir, "hub_strength_per_patient.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
g <- ggplot(hubs, aes(x = reorder(celltype, value, median), y = 100 * value, fill = role)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) + coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% of heterotypic communication", title = "Sender (out) and receiver (in) strength per patient") +
  theme_bw(10)
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "c_hub_strength.pdf"), g, width = 7, height = 5)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- (d) patient patterns
X <- enrichment_matrix(k$dir_norm)
pc <- prcomp(X)
ve <- summary(pc)$importance[2, ]
loadings <- as.data.frame(pc$rotation[, 1:3]); loadings$edge <- rownames(loadings)
write.csv(loadings[order(-abs(loadings$PC1)), ], file.path(out_dir, "pca_loadings_enrichment.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
pc_frac_cor <- cor(pc$x[, 1:3], k$Cmatrix, method = "spearman")
write.csv(round(pc_frac_cor, 3), file.path(out_dir, "pca_vs_cell_fractions_spearman.csv"))

set.seed(42)
cc <- consensus_cluster(X, ks = 2:6, reps = 500, p_item = 0.8)
cc_stats <- cc$stats
write.csv(cc_stats, file.path(out_dir, "consensus_clustering_stats.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
best_k <- choose_k(cc_stats, min_size = 5)
clusters <- cc$clusters[[as.character(best_k)]]
pattern_names <- name_patterns(clusters, X)
cl_df <- data.frame(patient = rownames(X), pattern = pattern_names[as.character(clusters)],
                    cluster = clusters, PC1 = pc$x[, 1], PC2 = pc$x[, 2],
                    consensus_membership = cc$membership[[as.character(best_k)]],
                    Response = meta$Response, Therapy = meta$Therapy)
write.csv(cl_df, file.path(out_dir, "patient_patterns.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(list(X = X, clusters = clusters, best_k = best_k, cc = cc, pattern_names = pattern_names),
        file.path(out_dir, "patient_patterns.rds"))

markers <- cluster_markers(X, k$dir_norm, clusters, pattern_names)
write.csv(markers, file.path(out_dir, "patient_pattern_marker_edges.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
comp <- aggregate(k$Cmatrix, list(pattern = pattern_names[as.character(clusters)]), median)
write.csv(comp, file.path(out_dir, "patient_pattern_median_cell_fractions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

g <- ggplot(cl_df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = pattern, shape = Response)) + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = sprintf("PC1 (%.0f%%)", 100 * ve[1]), y = sprintf("PC2 (%.0f%%)", 100 * ve[2]),
       title = "Patients by communication-enrichment profile") + theme_bw(10)
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "d1_pca_patient_patterns.pdf"), g, width = 7, height = 5)

ann <- data.frame(pattern = cl_df$pattern, Response = cl_df$Response, row.names = cl_df$patient)
top_var <- names(sort(apply(X, 2, var), decreasing = TRUE))[1:40]
ord <- order(cl_df$cluster, cl_df$PC1)
pheatmap(t(X[ord, top_var]), cluster_cols = FALSE, annotation_col = ann, show_colnames = FALSE,
         color = colorRampPalette(c("steelblue", "white", "firebrick"))(100),
         breaks = seq(-3, 3, length.out = 101), fontsize_row = 7,
         main = "z-scored log2 enrichment (40 most variable edges)",
         filename = file.path(fig_dir, "d2_heatmap_patient_patterns.pdf"), width = 9, height = 8)
pheatmap(cc$consensus[[as.character(best_k)]][ord, ord], cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE,
         annotation_col = ann, show_colnames = FALSE, show_rownames = FALSE,
         color = colorRampPalette(c("white", "navy"))(100),
         main = sprintf("Consensus matrix (k = %d, 500 x 80%% resamples)", best_k),
         filename = file.path(fig_dir, "d3_consensus_matrix.pdf"), width = 7, height = 6)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- (e) LR drivers
top_edges <- unique(c(head(hetero$edge[order(-hetero$median_prob)], 6),
                      head(hetero$edge[order(-hetero$frac_enriched, -hetero$median_enrichment)], 6),
                      head(markers$edge, 6)))
lr <- lr_drivers(input, top_edges, to_original_id(rownames(input$Cmatrix)), top_n = 8)
write.csv(lr, file.path(out_dir, "lr_drivers_top_edges.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
lr$label <- paste(lr$Ligand, lr$Receptor, sep = " - ")
g <- ggplot(lr, aes(x = edge, y = reorder(label, median_pct), size = median_pct, colour = frac_patients_present)) +
  geom_point() + scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "fraction of\npatients") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, size = "median %\nof edge", title = "Ligand-receptor pairs driving the most common edges") +
  theme_bw(9) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "e_lr_drivers.pdf"), g, width = 10, height = 9)

cat("Best k:", best_k, "\n"); print(table(cl_df$pattern))
print(cc_stats)
cat("\nTop 10 edges by median probability:\n")
print(head(edges[order(-edges$median_prob), c("edge", "median_prob", "frac_top10", "median_enrichment", "frac_enriched")], 10))
cat("\nTop 10 heterotypic edges by prevalence of enrichment:\n")
print(head(hetero[order(-hetero$frac_enriched, -hetero$median_enrichment),
                  c("edge", "median_prob", "median_enrichment", "frac_enriched")], 10))

# Pattern summarisation, clustering and LR-driver helpers (used by steps 3-4).

split_edge <- function(e) do.call(rbind, strsplit(e, "->", fixed = TRUE))

# Within-patient rank (1 = strongest) of every column.
row_ranks <- function(m) t(apply(-m, 1, rank, ties.method = "average"))

summarise_edges <- function(prob, enr, top_n = 10) {
  prob <- as.matrix(prob); enr <- as.matrix(enr[, colnames(prob)])
  rk <- row_ranks(prob)
  se <- split_edge(colnames(prob))
  out <- data.frame(
    edge = colnames(prob), sender = se[, 1], receiver = se[, 2],
    median_prob = apply(prob, 2, median),
    q25_prob = apply(prob, 2, quantile, 0.25), q75_prob = apply(prob, 2, quantile, 0.75),
    mean_rank = colMeans(rk), frac_top10 = colMeans(rk <= top_n),
    median_enrichment = apply(enr, 2, median),
    q25_enrichment = apply(enr, 2, quantile, 0.25), q75_enrichment = apply(enr, 2, quantile, 0.75),
    frac_enriched = colMeans(enr > 1),
    row.names = NULL
  )
  out[order(-out$median_prob), ]
}

summarise_features <- function(raw, nrm, top_n = 10) {
  rk <- row_ranks(raw)
  out <- data.frame(
    feature = colnames(raw),
    median_raw = apply(raw, 2, median),
    mean_rank = colMeans(rk), frac_top10 = colMeans(rk <= top_n),
    median_enrichment = apply(nrm, 2, median),
    frac_enriched = colMeans(nrm > 1),
    row.names = NULL
  )
  out[order(-out$frac_top10, -out$median_raw), ]
}

describe_motif <- function(f) {
  p <- strsplit(f, "_", fixed = TRUE)
  vapply(p, function(x) switch(x[1],
    W  = sprintf("%s -> %s -> %s (or reverse)", x[2], x[3], x[4]),
    TT = sprintf("%s -> %s -> %s, %s -> %s", x[2], x[3], x[4], x[2], x[4]),
    CT = sprintf("%s -> %s -> %s -> %s", x[2], x[3], x[4], x[2]),
    paste(x, collapse = "_")), character(1))
}

# Out-/in-strength of each cell type as a share of all heterotypic communication.
hub_strength <- function(prob, cts, exclude_self = TRUE) {
  se <- split_edge(colnames(prob))
  keep <- if (exclude_self) se[, 1] != se[, 2] else rep(TRUE, nrow(se))
  P <- prob[, keep, drop = FALSE]; se <- se[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  P <- P / rowSums(P)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(cts, function(ct) {
    rbind(data.frame(patient = rownames(P), celltype = ct, role = "sender (out)",
                     value = rowSums(P[, se[, 1] == ct, drop = FALSE])),
          data.frame(patient = rownames(P), celltype = ct, role = "receiver (in)",
                     value = rowSums(P[, se[, 2] == ct, drop = FALSE])))
  }))
}

enrichment_matrix <- function(enr) {
  X <- log2(as.matrix(enr))
  X <- X[, apply(X, 2, function(v) all(is.finite(v)) && sd(v) > 0), drop = FALSE]
  scale(X)
}

# Resampling-based consensus clustering (Monti et al. 2003) with Ward
# hierarchical clustering; ConsensusClusterPlus is not installed.
consensus_cluster <- function(X, ks = 2:6, reps = 500, p_item = 0.8) {
  n <- nrow(X); ids <- rownames(X)
  co_sampled <- matrix(0, n, n)
  co_clust <- lapply(ks, function(k) matrix(0, n, n)); names(co_clust) <- ks
  for (r in seq_len(reps)) {
    idx <- sort(sample(n, round(p_item * n)))
    h <- hclust(dist(X[idx, , drop = FALSE]), "ward.D2")
    co_sampled[idx, idx] <- co_sampled[idx, idx] + 1
    for (k in ks) {
      cl <- cutree(h, k)
      same <- outer(cl, cl, "==")
      co_clust[[as.character(k)]][idx, idx] <- co_clust[[as.character(k)]][idx, idx] + same
    }
  }
  consensus <- lapply(co_clust, function(m) { c <- m / pmax(co_sampled, 1); dimnames(c) <- list(ids, ids); c })
  clusters <- membership <- list()
  stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ks, function(k) {
    C <- consensus[[as.character(k)]]
    cl <- cutree(hclust(as.dist(1 - C), "average"), k)
    # relabel clusters by decreasing size so labels are reproducible
    relabel <- setNames(seq_along(table(cl)), names(sort(table(cl), decreasing = TRUE)))
    cl <- setNames(relabel[as.character(cl)], ids)
    clusters[[as.character(k)]] <<- cl
    membership[[as.character(k)]] <<- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) mean(C[i, cl == cl[i] & seq_len(n) != i]), numeric(1))
    lt <- C[lower.tri(C)]

hub_strength <- function(prob, cts, exclude_self = TRUE) {

# Resampling-based consensus clustering (Monti et al. 2003) with Ward
# hierarchical clustering; ConsensusClusterPlus is not installed.
consensus_cluster <- function(X, ks = 2:6, reps = 500, p_item = 0.8) {
  n <- nrow(X); ids <- rownames(X)
  co_sampled <- matrix(0, n, n)
  co_clust <- lapply(ks, function(k) matrix(0, n, n)); names(co_clust) <- ks
  for (r in seq_len(reps)) {
    idx <- sort(sample(n, round(p_item * n)))
    h <- hclust(dist(X[idx, , drop = FALSE]), "ward.D2")
    co_sampled[idx, idx] <- co_sampled[idx, idx] + 1
    for (k in ks) {
      cl <- cutree(h, k)
      same <- outer(cl, cl, "==")
      co_clust[[as.character(k)]][idx, idx] <- co_clust[[as.character(k)]][idx, idx] + same
    }
  }
  consensus <- lapply(co_clust, function(m) { c <- m / pmax(co_sampled, 1); dimnames(c) <- list(ids, ids); c })
  clusters <- membership <- list()
  stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ks, function(k) {
    C <- consensus[[as.character(k)]]
    cl <- cutree(hclust(as.dist(1 - C), "average"), k)
    # relabel clusters by decreasing size so labels are reproducible
    relabel <- setNames(seq_along(table(cl)), names(sort(table(cl), decreasing = TRUE)))
    cl <- setNames(relabel[as.character(cl)], ids)
    clusters[[as.character(k)]] <<- cl
    membership[[as.character(k)]] <<- vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) mean(C[i, cl == cl[i] & seq_len(n) != i]), numeric(1))
    lt <- C[lower.tri(C)]
    within <- mean(sapply(unique(cl), function(c) { m <- C[cl == c, cl == c]; mean(m[lower.tri(m)]) }), na.rm = TRUE)
    data.frame(k = k, PAC = mean(lt > 0.1 & lt < 0.9), mean_within_consensus = within,
               min_cluster_size = min(table(cl)),
               silhouette = mean(cluster::silhouette(cl, dist(X))[, 3]),
               sizes = paste(table(cl), collapse = "/"))
  }))
  list(stats = stats, clusters = clusters, consensus = consensus, membership = membership)
}

choose_k <- function(stats, min_size = 5) {
  ok <- stats[stats$min_cluster_size >= min_size, ]
  ok$k[which.min(ok$PAC)]
}

name_patterns <- function(clusters, X) setNames(paste0("P", sort(unique(clusters))), sort(unique(clusters)))

cluster_markers <- function(X, enr, clusters, pattern_names) {
  enr <- as.matrix(enr)[, colnames(X)]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(sort(unique(clusters)), function(c) {
    inn <- clusters == c
    res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(colnames(X), function(e) {
      w <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(X[inn, e], X[!inn, e]))
      data.frame(pattern = pattern_names[as.character(c)], edge = e,
                 median_enr_in = median(enr[inn, e]), median_enr_out = median(enr[!inn, e]),
                 log2FC = log2(median(enr[inn, e]) / median(enr[!inn, e])), p = w$p.value)
    }))
    res$FDR <- p.adjust(res$p, "BH")
    res[order(res$p), ]
  }))
}

# Ligand-receptor pairs that make up each directed edge (kernel is linear in
# LRmatrix, so contributions sum exactly to the edge's kernel score).
lr_drivers <- function(input, edges, pnames, top_n = 8) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(edges, function(e) {
    s <- split_edge(e)
    lr <- computeLRContributions(input$Lmatrix, input$Rmatrix, input$Cmatrix, input$LRmatrix,
                                 input$celltypes, sender = s[1], receiver = s[2], bundle = FALSE,
                                 patient_names = pnames)
    lr$pair <- paste(lr$Ligand, lr$Receptor, sep = "|")
    wide <- tapply(lr$PctOfTotal, list(lr$pair, lr$Patient), sum)
    wide[is.na(wide)] <- 0
    rk <- apply(-wide, 2, rank, ties.method = "min")
    agg <- data.frame(edge = e, pair = rownames(wide), median_pct = apply(wide, 1, median),
                      frac_top5 = rowMeans(rk <= 5), row.names = NULL)
    agg$frac_patients_present <- agg$frac_top5
    agg <- head(agg[order(-agg$median_pct), ], top_n)
    lrp <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(agg$pair, "|", fixed = TRUE))
    agg$Ligand <- lrp[, 1]; agg$Receptor <- lrp[, 2]
    agg
  }))
}

# prevalence of enrichment is only counted where the edge can actually exist.
edge_presence <- function(Cmatrix, edges) {
  se <- split_edge(edges)

  colnames(pres) <- edges

  do.call(rbind, lapply(edges, function(e) {
    s <- split_edge(e)
    lr <- computeLRContributions(input$Lmatrix, input$Rmatrix, input$Cmatrix, input$LRmatrix,
                                 input$celltypes, sender = s[1], receiver = s[2], bundle = FALSE,
                                 patient_names = pnames)
    lr$pair <- paste(lr$Ligand, lr$Receptor, sep = "|")
    wide <- tapply(lr$PctOfTotal, list(lr$pair, lr$Patient), sum)
    wide[is.na(wide)] <- 0
    rk <- apply(-wide, 2, rank, ties.method = "min")
    agg <- data.frame(edge = e, pair = rownames(wide), median_pct = apply(wide, 1, median),
                      frac_top5 = rowMeans(rk <= 5), row.names = NULL)
    agg$frac_patients_present <- agg$frac_top5
    agg <- head(agg[order(-agg$median_pct), ], top_n)
    lrp <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(agg$pair, "|", fixed = TRUE))
    agg$Ligand <- lrp[, 1]; agg$Receptor <- lrp[, 2]
    agg
  }))

# Step 1b: alternative RaCInG inputs using the curated cell-type/ligand and
# cell-type/receptor compatibility matrices of the original RaCInG publication
# (bundled with the package as `skcm_example`), instead of the data-driven
# NNLS profiles that prepare_input_files() derives from the cohort itself.

#  - LRmatrix: the curated LR pair set, weighted per patient by
#    min(log2(TPM+1)) of ligand and receptor (fun_LR = min, as in the package)
#  - Cmatrix: quanTIseq (B, M1+M2, NK, CD8, Treg, DC) + EPIC (CAF, Endo);
#    Tumor = quanTIseq "other" minus EPIC CAF + Endo (floored at 0);
#    renormalised over the 9 cell types. This approximates the TME-mod
#    composition of the original study.

work_dir <- normalizePath(if (length(args) >= 1) args[1] else ".")
source(file.path(work_dir, "scripts", "helpers.R"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(EPIC))

out_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "results", "01b_curated_prior_inputs")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

data(skcm_example, package = "RaCInG")
cur <- skcm_example
cur_cts <- c("B" = "B", "CAF" = "CAF", "CD8+ T" = "CD8", "DC" = "DC", "Endo" = "Endo",
             "M" = "Macrophage", "NK" = "NK", "Treg" = "Treg", "Tumor" = "Tumor")[cur$celltypes]
stopifnot(!is.unsorted(cur_cts))

tpm <- load_tpm(work_dir, rescale = TRUE)
log_tpm <- log2(tpm + 1)
q <- readRDS(file.path(work_dir, "results", "01_inputs", "quantiseq_fractions.rds"))

epic <- EPIC(bulk = tpm, reference = "TRef")$cellFractions
epic <- epic[rownames(q), ]
write.csv(cbind(sample = to_original_id(rownames(epic)), round(epic, 6)),
          file.path(out_dir, "epic_fractions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

C <- data.frame(
  B = q$B, CAF = epic[, "CAFs"], CD8 = q$CD8, DC = q$DC, Endo = epic[, "Endothelial"],
  Macrophage = q$M1 + q$M2, NK = q$NK, Treg = q$Treg,
  Tumor = pmax(q$Tumor - epic[, "CAFs"] - epic[, "Endothelial"], 0),
  row.names = rownames(q)
)
C <- as.matrix(C / rowSums(C))

# Curated LR pairs: every ligand-receptor combination that carries weight in
# any of the bundled example patients (970 pairs).
pairs <- which(apply(cur$LRmatrix > 0, c(1, 2), any), arr.ind = TRUE)

rec_gene <- gsub(".", "-", cur$receptors, fixed = TRUE)

  LR[pairs[r, 1], pairs[r, 2], ] <- pmin(log_tpm[l, ], log_tpm[rc, ])

for (p in seq_len(dim(LR)[3])) LR[, , p] <- LR[, , p] / sum(LR[, , p])

write.csv(cbind(sample = to_original_id(rownames(C)), round(C, 6)),
          file.path(out_dir, "Cmatrix_curated.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("Curated LR pairs:", nrow(pairs), " dropped (gene absent from Gide matrix):", n_missing, "\n")

# ---- agreement between data-driven (NNLS) and curated compatibility --------
main <- readRDS(file.path(work_dir, "results", "01_inputs", "Gide_RaCInG_input.rds"))
rownames(main$Lmatrix) <- rownames(main$Rmatrix) <- main$celltypes
match_ct <- list(B = "B", CD8 = "CD8", DC = "DC", NK = "NK", Treg = "Treg", Tumor = "Tumor",
                 Macrophage = c("M1", "M2"))
agree <- function(curM, mainM, cur_genes, main_genes, what) {
  colnames(curM) <- gsub(".", "-", cur_genes, fixed = TRUE)
  colnames(mainM) <- gsub(".", "-", main_genes, fixed = TRUE)
  genes <- intersect(colnames(curM), colnames(mainM))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(match_ct), function(ct) {
    a <- curM[ct, genes] > 0
    b <- apply(mainM[match_ct[[ct]], genes, drop = FALSE] > 0, 2, any)
    po <- mean(a == b); pe <- mean(a) * mean(b) + mean(!a) * mean(!b)
    data.frame(type = what, celltype = ct, shared_genes = length(genes),
               curated_pos = sum(a), data_driven_pos = sum(b), both = sum(a & b),
               jaccard = sum(a & b) / sum(a | b), cohen_kappa = (po - pe) / (1 - pe))
  }))
}
ag <- rbind(agree(Lm, main$Lmatrix, cur$ligands, colnames(main$Lmatrix), "ligand"),
            agree(Rm, main$Rmatrix, cur$receptors, colnames(main$Rmatrix), "receptor"))
write.csv(ag, file.path(out_dir, "compatibility_agreement_curated_vs_data_driven.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
print(ag, digits = 2)
cat("Median curated fractions:\n"); print(round(apply(C, 2, median), 3))

EdgetoAdj_No_loop <- function(E, N) {
  # E: two-column matrix where each row represents an edge (from, to)
  # N: total number of vertices
  # Returns: sparse adjacency matrix without self-loops (edges from a vertex to itself)
  
  # Step 1: Identify edges that are NOT self-loops
  # Keep only edges where the source and target are different
  keep <- E[,1] != E[,2]
  
  # Step 2: Filter the edge list to remove self-loops
  E_noloop <- E[keep,, drop = FALSE]
  
  # Step 3: Construct the sparse adjacency matrix
  # - i = source vertices
  # - j = target vertices
  # - x = 1 for each edge
  # - dims = N x N
  # This will sum duplicate edges automatically, if any
  Adj <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(
    i = E_noloop[,1], 
    j = E_noloop[,2], 
    x = rep(1, nrow(E_noloop)), 
    dims = c(N, N)
  )
  
  return(Adj)
}

# Step 4a: Monte Carlo RaCInG (explicit random graph realizations per patient)
# to check that the kernel (infinite-graph) features are reproduced by finite
# simulated networks, and how large graph-to-graph variability is.
# Usage: Rscript 04a_montecarlo.R <work_dir> <input.rds> <out_dir> <types,comma> <Ncells> <Ngraphs> <Ndegree> <norm> <ncores>
args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
work_dir <- normalizePath(args[1])
source(file.path(work_dir, "scripts", "helpers.R"))
input   <- readRDS(args[2])
out_dir <- args[3]
types   <- strsplit(args[4], ",")[[1]]
Ncells  <- as.integer(args[5]); Ngraphs <- as.integer(args[6]); Ndegree <- as.numeric(args[7])
norm    <- as.logical(args[8]); ncores <- as.integer(args[9])
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

set.seed(2024)
t0 <- Sys.time()
mc <- compute_racing_montecarlo(
  input_data = input, output_folder = out_dir, file_name = "Gide_MC",
  communication_type = types, Ncells = Ncells, Ngraphs = Ngraphs, Ndegree = Ndegree,
  remove_direction = FALSE, norm = norm, ncores = ncores
)
cat("Monte Carlo finished in", format(Sys.time() - t0), "\n")
mc$settings <- list(types = types, Ncells = Ncells, Ngraphs = Ngraphs, Ndegree = Ndegree, norm = norm)
saveRDS(mc, file.path(out_dir, "montecarlo_results.rds"))

# Builder for the curated-prior RaCInG configuration (see 01b_curated_prior_inputs.R).

curated_prior <- function() {
  data(skcm_example, package = "RaCInG", envir = environment())
  cur <- skcm_example
  cts <- c("B" = "B", "CAF" = "CAF", "CD8+ T" = "CD8", "DC" = "DC", "Endo" = "Endo",
           "M" = "Macrophage", "NK" = "NK", "Treg" = "Treg", "Tumor" = "Tumor")[cur$celltypes]
  stopifnot(!is.unsorted(cts))
  Lm <- cur$Lmatrix; Rm <- cur$Rmatrix
  dimnames(Lm) <- list(unname(cts), cur$ligands); dimnames(Rm) <- list(unname(cts), cur$receptors)
  # every LR combination carrying weight in any bundled example patient
  pairs <- which(apply(cur$LRmatrix > 0, c(1, 2), any), arr.ind = TRUE)
  list(Lmatrix = Lm, Rmatrix = Rm, celltypes = unname(cts), ligands = cur$ligands,
       receptors = cur$receptors, pairs = pairs,
       lig_gene = gsub(".", "-", cur$ligands, fixed = TRUE),
       rec_gene = gsub(".", "-", cur$receptors, fixed = TRUE))
}

run_epic <- function(tpm) EPIC::EPIC(bulk = tpm, reference = "TRef")$cellFractions

# tumor_mode: "subtract" (Tumor = quanTIseq other - EPIC CAF - EPIC Endo) or
# "other" (Tumor = quanTIseq other, CAF/Endo added on top, then renormalised)
curated_cmatrix <- function(q, epic, tumor_mode = "subtract") {
  epic <- epic[rownames(q), ]
  tumor <- if (tumor_mode == "subtract") pmax(q$Tumor - epic[, "CAFs"] - epic[, "Endothelial"], 0) else q$Tumor
  C <- data.frame(B = q$B, CAF = epic[, "CAFs"], CD8 = q$CD8, DC = q$DC, Endo = epic[, "Endothelial"],
                  Macrophage = q$M1 + q$M2, NK = q$NK, Treg = q$Treg, Tumor = tumor,
                  row.names = rownames(q))
  as.matrix(C / rowSums(C))
}

curated_lrmatrix <- function(prior, log_tpm, keep_pairs = NULL) {
  pairs <- prior$pairs
  if (!is.null(keep_pairs)) pairs <- pairs[keep_pairs, , drop = FALSE]
  LR <- array(0, dim = c(length(prior$ligands), length(prior$receptors), ncol(log_tpm)))
  n_missing <- 0
  for (r in seq_len(nrow(pairs))) {
    l <- prior$lig_gene[pairs[r, 1]]; rc <- prior$rec_gene[pairs[r, 2]]
    if (!(l %in% rownames(log_tpm) && rc %in% rownames(log_tpm))) { n_missing <- n_missing + 1; next }
    LR[pairs[r, 1], pairs[r, 2], ] <- pmin(log_tpm[l, ], log_tpm[rc, ])
  }
  for (p in seq_len(dim(LR)[3])) LR[, , p] <- LR[, , p] / sum(LR[, , p])
  attr(LR, "n_missing") <- n_missing
  LR
}

build_curated_input <- function(prior, tpm, q, epic, tumor_mode = "subtract", keep_pairs = NULL) {
  C <- curated_cmatrix(q, epic, tumor_mode)
  LR <- curated_lrmatrix(prior, log2(tpm[, rownames(C), drop = FALSE] + 1), keep_pairs)
  list(Lmatrix = prior$Lmatrix, Rmatrix = prior$Rmatrix, Cmatrix = C, LRmatrix = LR,
       celltypes = prior$celltypes, ligands = prior$ligands, receptors = prior$receptors)
}

agree <- function(curM, mainM, cur_genes, main_genes, what) {
  colnames(curM) <- gsub(".", "-", cur_genes, fixed = TRUE)
  colnames(mainM) <- gsub(".", "-", main_genes, fixed = TRUE)
  genes <- intersect(colnames(curM), colnames(mainM))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(match_ct), function(ct) {
    a <- curM[ct, genes] > 0
    b <- apply(mainM[match_ct[[ct]], genes, drop = FALSE] > 0, 2, any)
    po <- mean(a == b); pe <- mean(a) * mean(b) + mean(!a) * mean(!b)
    data.frame(type = what, celltype = ct, shared_genes = length(genes),
               curated_pos = sum(a), data_driven_pos = sum(b), both = sum(a & b),
               jaccard = sum(a & b) / sum(a | b), cohen_kappa = (po - pe) / (1 - pe))
